label: thm:main
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:main}
Let Assumption~\ref{ass:class} hold and let $0<c_-\le c_+$. There are $\varepsilon_0,c_1,C_1>0$ and
$C_{\mathrm{dim}}\ge32$, depending only on the constants of Assumption~\ref{ass:class} and on $c_\pm$, with the
following property. If $0<\varepsilon\le\varepsilon_0$, $c_-n_{\varepsilon}\le n\le c_+n_{\varepsilon}$ and $d\geC_{\mathrm{dim}}\max\{n,n_{\varepsilon}\}$,
then every proper learner that is $\varepsilon$-accurate on the family satisfies, for each $\mathcal{Q}$ and every
$\tau\ge0$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:main}
 c_1\frac n{1+(\tau/\varepsilon)^2}\le\sup_{p}\mathcal{Q}_{D_p}(X+\tau G)\le C_1\frac n{1+(\tau/\varepsilon)^2},
\end{equation}
where $p$ ranges over $[-1,1]^d$. The lower bound holds on average over a beta prior on $p$ that does
not depend on the learner (Section~\ref{sec:architecture}), and the upper bound holds at every $p$. Both
bounds hold for the infimum over any nonempty class of such learners.

\label{prop:samples}
Under Assumption~\ref{ass:class}, projected stochastic gradient descent in epochs (epoch SGD) is a
proper learner that is $\varepsilon$-accurate on
every distribution on the unit ball with $O(n_{\varepsilon})$ samples. Conversely, if $d\geC_{\mathrm{dim}}n_{\varepsilon}$ and $\varepsilon$
is small enough, every proper learner that is $\varepsilon$-accurate on the family uses $\Omega(n_{\varepsilon})$
samples.

label: eq:noisy-bound
title: Remark
body_md:
Seen through noise at the scale of their range, the loss differences give a bound of the right order,
which Cauchy--Schwarz also gives without information.
Let $Y=X+\tau G$ with $\tau>0$. Then $\mathbb{E}_p\sigma_iY_i=\mathbb{E}_p\sigma_iX_i$, and as $|X_i|\le2L$, $\sigma_iY_i$
is sub-Gaussian with variance proxy $s^2=4L^2+\tau^2$ when $U_i$ is drawn independently of $Y_i$. The
decoupling estimate of \citet{russo2016} and \citet{xu2017}, Cauchy--Schwarz and \eqref{eq:hierarchy}
give, at every law,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:noisy-bound}
\begin{aligned}
 |\mathrm{gen}_p|&\le\frac1n\sum_i\sqrt{2\ln2\,s^2I_{D_p}(Y_i;U_i)}\\
 &\le\big(2\ln2\,s^2\,\mathcal{I}^{\mathrm{cand}}_{D_p}(Y)/n\big)^{1/2}.
\end{aligned}
\end{equation}
At $\tau=2L$, \eqref{eq:upper} and Proposition~\ref{prop:finite} bound the right side by
$(2C_{\mathrm{res}})^{1/2}\varepsilon$ at every law for every learner of Theorem~\ref{thm:main}. This is the order of
the gap on prior average, and $\sqrt2$ times the bound $C_{\mathrm{res}}^{1/2}\varepsilon$ on $|\mathrm{gen}_p|$ that
Cauchy--Schwarz gives without information, as $\mathbb{E}_p\sigma_iX_{p,i}^*(\widetilde Z)=0$. For ridge ERM, in our runs
at $d=32n$ and $d=64n$, the resulting bound is at most $1.44$ times the gap on prior average
(Appendix~\ref{app:noisy-bound}).

Under the hypotheses of Theorem~\ref{thm:main}, let $\Pi=\Pi_\kappa$ with $v=(4\varepsilon/\beta)^{2/q}$.
There are $c_M,C_V,C_{\mathrm{res}}>0$, depending only on the constants of Assumption~\ref{ass:class}

$\sum_i\mathbb{E}_\Pi\sigma_iX_i\ge c_Mn\varepsilon$ and $\sum_i\mathbb{E}_\Pi X_i^2\le C_Vn\varepsilon^2$, and
$\mathbb{E}_p\lVertX-X_p^*(\widetilde Z)\rVert^2\le C_{\mathrm{res}}n\varepsilon^2$ at every $p$, where the reference
$X_{p,i}^*(\widetilde Z)=\phi(\langle\theta_p^*,Z_{1,i}\rangle)-\phi(\langle\theta_p^*,Z_{0,i}\rangle)$ is the release of the
population minimizer.

title: Conventions
body_md:
Information is measured in bits; $\ln$ is the natural logarithm and $\log_2$ the binary one, and a
quantity computed in nats is divided by $\ln2$ before it is compared with bits. $\mathbb{E}_p$ and $\mathbb{P}_p$
are taken when the data law is $D_p$, over the candidates, the selection bits, the learner's seed $R$
and the noise $G$. $\mathbb{E}_\Pi$ and $\mathbb{P}_\Pi$ first draw $p$ from a prior $\Pi$, which is the beta prior
$\Pi_\kappa$ unless stated otherwise, and then take $\mathbb{E}_p$ and $\mathbb{P}_p$; $I_{D_p}$ denotes mutual
information when the data law is $D_p$. The norm $\lVert\cdot\rVert$ is Euclidean, $\lVert\cdot\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}$ is the
operator norm, $\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle$ is the Euclidean inner product and ${}^\top$ denotes the transpose.
Entropies are set in roman type: $\mathrm{H}$ is Shannon entropy, $\mathrm{h}$ is differential entropy and
$\mathrm{h}_2$ is the binary entropy function in bits, while the italic $H$ is always the curvature bound of
the link. The index $i\in[n]$ labels pairs, $j\in\{0,1\}$ the candidate within a pair and $k\in[d]$
coordinates; the coordinate index comes last, as in $Z_{j,i,k}$. The symbols $O$, $\Omega$, $\Theta$,
$\asymp$ and $\lesssim$ hide constants that depend only on the constants of
Assumption~\ref{ass:class} and on $c_\pm$.

\[

head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Fix a coordinate $k$ and the other coordinates $p_{-k}$ of $p$; until the last step, all
expectations are conditional on $p_{-k}$. For $z=(z_1,\dots,z_n)\in\mathcal Z^n$,
\[
 \mathbb{P}_p(S_n=z)=\prod_{i=1}^n\prod_{k'=1}^d\frac{1+\sqrt d\,p_{k'}z_{i,k'}}2 .
\]
Let $\bar\theta_k(z)=\mathbb{E}[\widehat\theta_k\mid S_n=z]$ be the $k$-th output coordinate averaged over the seed; it
is bounded, and it does not depend on $p$ because $R$ is independent of $p$ and of the data. Since
$\mathcal Z^n$ is finite and each factor above is affine in $p_k$, the function
\[
 \Upsilon_k(t)=\mathbb{E}[\widehat\theta_k\mid p_k=t]=\sum_{z\in\mathcal Z^n}\bar\theta_k(z)\,\mathbb{P}_p(S_n=z)\big|_{p_k=t}
\]
is a polynomial of degree at most $n$. For $|t|<1$ and $z_{i,k}=\pm1/\sqrt d$,
\[
 \frac{\partial}{\partial t}\ln\frac{1+\sqrt d\,t\,z_{i,k}}2
 =\frac{\sqrt d\,z_{i,k}}{1+\sqrt d\,t\,z_{i,k}}
 =\frac{\sqrt d\,(z_{i,k}-t/\sqrt d)}{1-t^2},
\]
as one checks separately for the two signs. Since $\mu_{p,k}=p_k/\sqrt d$, differentiating the
likelihood term by term gives
\[
 (1-t^2)\,\Upsilon_k'(t)=\sqrt d\;\mathbb{E}\Big[\bar\theta_k(S_n)\sum_{i=1}^n(Z_{U_i,i,k}-\mu_{p,k})\Bigm|p_k=t\Big]
 =\sqrt d\;\mathbb{E}\Big[\widehat\theta_k\sum_{i=1}^n(Z_{U_i,i,k}-\mu_{p,k})\Bigm|p_k=t\Big].
\]
Now apply \eqref{eq:prior-ibp} with $\Upsilon=\Upsilon_k$. Its left side is
$\kappa\mathbb{E}[p_k\widehat\theta_k]=\kappa\sqrt d\,\mathbb{E}[\mu_{p,k}\widehat\theta_k]$, and its right side is
$\sqrt d\,\mathbb{E}[\widehat\theta_k\sum_i(Z_{U_i,i,k}-\mu_{p,k})]$. Dividing by $\sqrt d$, averaging over $p_{-k}$ and
summing over $k$ proves the lemma. The argument uses only $\kappa>0$; $\kappa$ need not be an integer.

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $\eta_0=1/30$ and $\lambda_0=19/80$, so that $1+2/\eta_0=61$, $1-2\lambda_0=21/40$ and
$2\lambda_0(1-\eta_0)^2=c_{\mathrm{net}}$. Given $p$, the training points are independent draws from $D_p$, so
the entries $Z_{U_i,i,k}-\mu_{p,k}$ of $B_{\mathrm{tr}}$ are independent and centred, and each takes values in an
interval of length $2/\sqrt d$.

Fix $x$ in the unit sphere $\mathbb S^{n-1}$ of $\mathbb{R}^n$. The $k$-th coordinate of $B_{\mathrm{tr}}^\top x$ is
$\sum_ix_i(Z_{U_i,i,k}-\mu_{p,k})$, and its $i$-th term takes values in an interval of length
$2|x_i|/\sqrt d$. By Hoeffding's lemma, $\mathbb{E}_p\exp\{t'(B_{\mathrm{tr}}^\top x)_k\}\le\exp\{t'^2\sum_ix_i^2/(2d)\}
=e^{t'^2/(2d)}$ for every real $t'$. Since
$(2\pi)^{-1/2}\int_\mathbb{R}\exp\{\sqrt{2\lambda_0d}\,yx'-y^2/2\}\,dy=e^{\lambda_0dx'^2}$ for every real $x'$,
Fubini's theorem and this bound with $t'=\sqrt{2\lambda_0d}\,y$ give
\[
 \mathbb{E}_p\exp\{\lambda_0d(B_{\mathrm{tr}}^\top x)_k^2\}
 \le\frac1{\sqrt{2\pi}}\int_\mathbb{R} e^{\lambda_0y^2-y^2/2}\,dy=(1-2\lambda_0)^{-1/2}.
\]
The coordinates of $B_{\mathrm{tr}}^\top x$ involve disjoint columns of $B_{\mathrm{tr}}$ and are therefore independent, so
$\mathbb{E}_p\exp\{\lambda_0d\lVertB_{\mathrm{tr}}^\top x\rVert^2\}\le(1-2\lambda_0)^{-d/2}$.

Let $\mathcal S\subset\mathbb S^{n-1}$ be an $\eta_0$-net of the sphere with
$|\mathcal S|\le(1+2/\eta_0)^n$, which exists by a volume argument. If $x^\star\in\mathbb S^{n-1}$
satisfies $\lVertB_{\mathrm{tr}}^\top x^\star\rVert=\lVertB_{\mathrm{tr}}\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}$ and $x\in\mathcal S$ satisfies
$\lVertx-x^\star\rVert\le\eta_0$, then $\lVertB_{\mathrm{tr}}\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}\le\lVertB_{\mathrm{tr}}^\top x\rVert+\eta_0\lVertB_{\mathrm{tr}}\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}$. Hence
$(1-\eta_0)^2\lVertB_{\mathrm{tr}}\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}^2\le\max_{x\in\mathcal S}\lVertB_{\mathrm{tr}}^\top x\rVert^2$, and bounding the maximum by
the sum over the net,
\[
 \mathbb{E}_p\exp\{\lambda_0d(1-\eta_0)^2\lVertB_{\mathrm{tr}}\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}^2\}\le(1+2/\eta_0)^n(1-2\lambda_0)^{-d/2}.
\]
By the choice of $\eta_0$ and $\lambda_0$, the logarithm of the right side equals
$n\ln61+\frac d2\ln(40/21)=K_0/K_1$, and $\lambda_0d(1-\eta_0)^2=c_{\mathrm{net}} d/2=1/K_1$. Jensen's inequality
for the exponential function gives
$\mathbb{E}_p\lVertB_{\mathrm{tr}}\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}^2\le K_1\ln\mathbb{E}_p\exp\{\lVertB_{\mathrm{tr}}\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}^2/K_1\}\le K_0$, and Markov's inequality gives, for
$t\ge0$,
\[
 \mathbb{P}_p\big(\lVertB_{\mathrm{tr}}\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}^2>K_0+K_1t\big)\le\exp\{K_0/K_1-(K_0+K_1t)/K_1\}=e^{-t}.
\]

The entries $Z_{1,i,k}-Z_{0,i,k}$ of $\Delta$ are independent and centred, and each is the sum of the
two independent centred terms $Z_{1,i,k}-\mu_{p,k}$ and $-(Z_{0,i,k}-\mu_{p,k})$, with values in
intervals of length $2/\sqrt d$. Hoeffding's lemma, applied to both terms, gives
$\mathbb{E}_p\exp\{t'(\Delta^\top x)_k\}\le e^{t'^2/d}$, so the matrix $\Delta/\sqrt2$ satisfies the bound used
above for $B_{\mathrm{tr}}$. The rest of the argument applies verbatim and gives
$\mathbb{P}_p(\lVert\Delta\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}^2/2>K_0+K_1t)\le e^{-t}$.

title: Proof
body_md:
If $K_1=0$, letting $t\to\infty$ in the tail bound shows $N\le K_0$ almost surely, so
$\mathbb{E}[N\omega]\le K_0w$. Otherwise let $t^\star=K_0+K_1\ln(\bar\omega/w)$, which is at least $K_0\ge0$
because $w\le\bar\omega$. Pointwise,
$N\omega\le t^\star\omega+\bar\omega(N-t^\star)_+$: if $N\le t^\star$ this holds because $\omega\ge0$,
and otherwise $(N-t^\star)\omega\le(N-t^\star)\bar\omega$. Integrating the tail bound,
\[
 \mathbb{E}(N-t^\star)_+=\int_0^\infty\mathbb{P}(N>t^\star+y)\,dy
 \le\int_0^\infty\frac w{\bar\omega}\,e^{-y/K_1}\,dy=\frac{K_1w}{\bar\omega}.
\]
Hence $\mathbb{E}[N\omega]\le t^\star\mathbb{E}\omega+K_1w\le t^\star w+K_1w=\mathfrak{T}_{\bar\omega}(w;K_0,K_1)$.

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $Y=X+\tau G$ and fix $p$. Under $D_p$ each $U_i$ is a fair bit, because $U$ is uniform and
independent of $p$, and $\mathbb{E}_pY_i^2<\infty$ for $\Pi$-almost every $p$ by the energy bound. Applying
\eqref{eq:fairbit} to $(Y_i,U_i)$ under $D_p$ and summing over $i$,
\[
 \mathcal{I}^{\mathrm{ind}}_{D_p}(Y)\ge\frac1{2\ln2}\sum_{i=1}^n\frac{(\mathbb{E}_p\sigma_iY_i)^2}{\mathbb{E}_pY_i^2},
\]
where a term with a vanishing denominator is zero. Average over $p\sim\Pi$ and apply the
Cauchy--Schwarz inequality in the form $\int x^2/y\ge(\int x)^2/\int y$, for $y>0$, to the functions
$x=\mathbb{E}_p\sigma_iY_i$ and $y=\mathbb{E}_pY_i^2$ of the pair $(p,i)$:
\[
 \mathbb{E}_\Pi\mathcal{I}^{\mathrm{ind}}_{D_p}(Y)\ge\frac{\big(\sum_i\mathbb{E}_\Pi\sigma_iY_i\big)^2}{2\ln2\,\sum_i\mathbb{E}_\Pi Y_i^2}.
\]
Since $G$ is independent of $(p,\widetilde Z,U,X)$ and its coordinates are centred with unit variance,
$\mathbb{E}_p\sigma_iY_i=\mathbb{E}_p\sigma_iX_i$ and $\mathbb{E}_pY_i^2=\mathbb{E}_pX_i^2+\tau^2$. The hypotheses of part~(a) give
$\sum_i\mathbb{E}_\Pi\sigma_iY_i\ge M>0$ and $\sum_i\mathbb{E}_\Pi Y_i^2\le V+n\tau^2$, which proves \eqref{eq:lower}.

title: Proof
body_md:
Fix $p$ and $\tau>0$, let $Y=X+\tau G$, and measure information and differential entropy in nats until
the last step. Given $\widetilde Z$, $U\to X\to Y$ is a Markov chain, because $G$ is independent of
$(\widetilde Z,U,X)$. Conditional data processing gives
$I(Y;U\mid\widetilde Z)\le I(Y;X\mid\widetilde Z)=\mathrm{h}(Y\mid\widetilde Z)-\mathrm{h}(Y\mid X,\widetilde Z)$, and
$\mathrm{h}(Y\mid X,\widetilde Z)=\mathrm{h}(\tau G)=\frac n2\ln(2\pi e\tau^2)$. Given $\widetilde Z$, subtracting the
reference $x_p(\widetilde Z)$ is an invertible translation, so $\mathrm{h}(Y\mid\widetilde Z)=\mathrm{h}(Y-x_p(\widetilde Z)\mid\widetilde Z)$.
Whatever its mean, a real random variable has differential entropy at most that of the centred
Gaussian law with the same second moment. By subadditivity of differential entropy and this bound for
each coordinate given $\widetilde Z$,
\[
 \mathrm{h}(Y\mid\widetilde Z)\le\sum_{i=1}^n\mathrm{h}\big(Y_i-x_{p,i}(\widetilde Z)\bigm|\widetilde Z\big)
 \le\sum_{i=1}^n\mathbb{E}\,\tfrac12\ln\Big(2\pi e\,\mathbb{E}\big[(Y_i-x_{p,i}(\widetilde Z))^2\bigm|\widetilde Z\big]\Big),
\]
and $\mathbb{E}[(Y_i-x_{p,i}(\widetilde Z))^2\mid\widetilde Z]=\mathbb{E}[(X_i-x_{p,i}(\widetilde Z))^2\mid\widetilde Z]+\tau^2$. Jensen's inequality for
the logarithm, over the coordinates and over $\widetilde Z$, then gives
\[
 I(Y;U\mid\widetilde Z)\le\frac12\sum_{i=1}^n\mathbb{E}\ln\Big(1+\frac{\mathbb{E}[(X_i-x_{p,i}(\widetilde Z))^2\mid\widetilde Z]}{\tau^2}\Big)
 \le\frac n2\ln\Big(1+\frac{\mathbb{E}_p\lVertX-x_p(\widetilde Z)\rVert^2}{n\tau^2}\Big)
 \le\frac n2\ln\Big(1+\frac{V_{\mathrm{res}}}{n\tau^2}\Big).
\]
The reference need not be the conditional mean of $X$ given $\widetilde Z$. Dividing by $\ln2$ gives the
second term of \eqref{eq:upper} in bits. The first term, and the bound $\mathcal{I}^{\mathrm{cand}}_{D_p}(X)\le n$ at
$\tau=0$, hold because $I(Y;U\mid\widetilde Z)\le\mathrm{H}(U\mid\widetilde Z)=\mathrm{H}(U)=n$ bits for every $\tau\ge0$.

title: Proof
body_md:
For real $x$, $|x-\lambda\operatorname{clip}(x/\lambda,-1,1)|=(|x|-\lambda)_+\le x^2/(4\lambda)$; when
$|x|\ge\lambda$, the inequality is $(|x|-2\lambda)^2\ge0$. As
$\mathbb{E}[\hat\sigma_i\mid X,U]=\operatorname{clip}(X_i/\lambda,-1,1)$,
\[
 \lambda\,\mathbb{E}_\Pi\sigma_i\hat\sigma_i=\mathbb{E}_\Pi\big[\sigma_i\lambda\operatorname{clip}(X_i/\lambda,-1,1)\big]
 \ge\mathbb{E}_\Pi\sigma_iX_i-\frac{\mathbb{E}_\Pi X_i^2}{4\lambda}.
\]
Summing over $i$ and using the two moment bounds, $\sum_i\mathbb{E}_\Pi\sigma_i\hat\sigma_i\ge
M/\lambda-V/(4\lambda^2)=M^2/V$ at $\lambda=V/(2M)$. Since $\sigma_i\hat\sigma_i=1$ exactly when
$\widehat U_i=U_i$, we have $\mathbb{P}_\Pi(\widehat U_i=U_i)=(1+\mathbb{E}_\Pi\sigma_i\hat\sigma_i)/2$, which proves the
first bound in \eqref{eq:bitguarantee}.

For the second, let $t_i=\mathbb{E}_\Pi\sigma_i\hat\sigma_i$. Under $\mathbb{P}_\Pi$ the bit $U_i$ is fair and the guess
$\widehat U_i$ errs with probability $(1-t_i)/2$. Fano's inequality for a binary guess holds whatever
the error probability, and since $\mathsf{J}$ is even it gives $I_\Pi(\hat\sigma_i;U_i)\ge1-\mathrm{h}_2((1-t_i)/2)=\mathsf{J}(t_i)$.
Since $p$ is independent of $U_i$,
$I_\Pi(\hat\sigma_i;U_i)\le I_\Pi(\hat\sigma_i,p;U_i)=I_\Pi(\hat\sigma_i;U_i\mid p)=\mathbb{E}_\Pi I_{D_p}(\hat\sigma_i;U_i)$.
By convexity of $\mathsf{J}$, $\sum_i\mathsf{J}(t_i)\ge n\mathsf{J}(\bar t)$ with $\bar t=n^{-1}\sum_it_i\ge M^2/(nV)$. The
Cauchy--Schwarz inequality gives
$M^2\le(\sum_i\mathbb{E}_\Pi\sigma_iX_i)^2\le n\sum_i\mathbb{E}_\Pi X_i^2\le nV$, so $M^2/(nV)\in(0,1]$, and since $\mathsf{J}$
is increasing on $[0,1]$, $n\mathsf{J}(\bar t)\ge n\mathsf{J}(M^2/(nV))$. Together these bounds prove
\eqref{eq:bitguarantee}.

label: rem:noisy-model
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:noisy-model}
Let $G'\sim\mathcal{N}(0,I_d)$ be independent of the data, the selection bits and the learner. Under
Assumption~\ref{ass:class}, for every $p\in[-1,1]^d$, every proper learner that is $\varepsilon$-accurate at
$D_p$ and every $\tau>0$,
\[
 I_{D_p}(\widehat\theta+\tau G';U\mid\widetilde Z)\le\min\Big\{n,\frac w{2\ln2\,\tau^2}\Big\},\qquad
 w=\min\{4,(\varepsilon/a_-)^{2/r}\}.
\]
Indeed, $\mathbb{E}_p\lVert\widehat\theta-\theta_p^*\rVert^2\le w$ by \eqref{eq:error}, whose proof uses accuracy at $D_p$
only, and $\theta_p^*$ is fixed once $p$ is. Given $\widetilde Z$, $U\to\widehat\theta\to\widehat\theta+\tau G'$ is a Markov chain,
and the proof of the Gaussian upper bound in Appendix~\ref{app:hierarchy}, in dimension $d$ and with
the reference $\theta_p^*$, bounds the information by
$\frac d2\ln(1+w/(d\tau^2))\le w/(2\tau^2)$ nats, and the bound $n$ holds because $U$ takes $2^n$
values.

In the sample-size range of Theorem~\ref{thm:main}, $n\ge c_-n_{\varepsilon}$ gives
$w\le(\varepsilon/a_-)^{2/r}\le n\varepsilon^2/(c_-a_-^{2/r})$, so the information of the perturbed model is at most
\[
 \min\Big\{n,\frac{n\varepsilon^2}{2\ln2\,c_-a_-^{2/r}\tau^2}\Big\}
 \le\Big(1+\frac1{2\ln2\,c_-a_-^{2/r}}\Big)\frac n{1+(\tau/\varepsilon)^2}.
\]

a constant that does not contain the factor $2K_0(L+H)^2$ of $V_{\mathrm{res}}$.

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $0<\varepsilon\le\varepsilon_0$, let $n$ and $d$ be as above, and let $\widehat\theta$ be a proper learner that is
$\varepsilon$-accurate on the family. The prior $\Pi_\kappa$ is fixed before the learner, $p$ is drawn
independently of the selection bits, the seed and the noise, and the reference $X_p^*(\widetilde Z)$ depends
only on $p$ and the candidates. By
Proposition~\ref{prop:finite}, Theorem~\ref{thm:transfer} applies with the reference
$x_p=X_p^*$ and with $M\ge c_Mn\varepsilon>0$, $V\le C_Vn\varepsilon^2$ and $V_{\mathrm{res}}\le C_{\mathrm{res}}n\varepsilon^2$. Its
lower bound \eqref{eq:lower} gives, for every $\tau\ge0$,
\[
 \mathbb{E}_\Pi\mathcal{I}^{\mathrm{ind}}_{D_p}(X+\tau G)
 \ge\frac{M^2}{2\ln2\,(V+n\tau^2)}
 \ge\frac{c_M^2}{2\ln2}\,\frac n{C_V+(\tau/\varepsilon)^2}
 \ge c_1\frac n{1+(\tau/\varepsilon)^2},\qquad
 c_1=\frac{c_M^2}{2\ln2\,\max\{C_V,1\}},
\]
since $C_V+x\le\max\{C_V,1\}(1+x)$ for $x\ge0$. Its upper bound \eqref{eq:upper} gives, at every $p$
and for $\tau>0$, with $a=C_{\mathrm{res}}/(2\ln2)$ and $x=(\tau/\varepsilon)^2$,
\[
 \mathcal{I}^{\mathrm{cand}}_{D_p}(X+\tau G)
 \le n\min\Big\{1,\frac{\ln\big(1+C_{\mathrm{res}}(\varepsilon/\tau)^2\big)}{2\ln2}\Big\}
 \le n\min\Big\{1,\frac ax\Big\}
 \le(1+a)\frac n{1+x},
\]
by $\ln(1+y)\le y$ and by the inequality $\min\{1,a/x\}\le(1+a)/(1+x)$, which holds for $a\ge0$ and
$x>0$ (consider the cases $x\le a$ and $x>a$). At $\tau=0$, Theorem~\ref{thm:transfer} gives
$\mathcal{I}^{\mathrm{cand}}_{D_p}(X)\le\mathrm{H}(U\mid\widetilde Z)=n$. So $\mathcal{I}^{\mathrm{cand}}_{D_p}(X+\tau G)\le C_1n/(1+(\tau/\varepsilon)^2)$ for every
$\tau\ge0$ and every $p$, with $C_1=1+C_{\mathrm{res}}/(2\ln2)$.

By \eqref{eq:hierarchy}, $\mathcal{I}^{\mathrm{ind}}\le\mathcal{I}^{\mathrm{joint}}\le\mathcal{I}^{\mathrm{cand}}$ at every $p$. So the lower bound holds for all three
information measures on average over the prior, and the upper bound holds for all three at every $p$. A prior
average is at most the supremum over $p$, which gives both bounds of \eqref{eq:main} for
$\sup_p\mathcal{Q}_{D_p}(X+\tau G)$, for each $\mathcal{Q}\in\{\mathcal{I}^{\mathrm{ind}},\mathcal{I}^{\mathrm{joint}},\mathcal{I}^{\mathrm{cand}}\}$ and every $\tau\ge0$. The constants
$\varepsilon_0$, $c_1$, $C_1$ and $C_{\mathrm{dim}}$ depend only on the constants of Assumption~\ref{ass:class} and on
$c_\pm$, not on the learner, so both bounds also hold for the infimum over any nonempty class of such
learners. This proves Theorem~\ref{thm:main}. The maximizing law may depend on the learner, on $\mathcal{Q}$
and on $\tau$.

title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:reflection}
Let $\phi$ satisfy the link conditions of Assumption~\ref{ass:class} ($\phi$ is convex and $C^2$ on a
neighbourhood of $[-1,1]$, $|\phi'|\le L$ and $0\le\phi''\le H$ on $[-1,1]$) except that
$\phi'(0)>0$, and put $b=\phi'(0)$. Write $\phi^-(t)=\phi(-t)$, and for a proper learner $A_n$ let
$A_n^-(S_n;R)=A_n(-S_n;R)$, where $-S_n$ negates every training point. Write $X^{A,\phi}$ for the
release of Definition~\ref{def:release} of the learner $A_n$ with the link $\phi$. Then:
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] $\phi^-$ satisfies the link conditions of Assumption~\ref{ass:class} with the same $b$, $L$
and $H$;
\item[(ii)] if $A_n$ is $\varepsilon$-accurate on the family for $f=g+\phi(\langle\theta,z\rangle)$, then $A_n^-$ is a
proper learner that is $\varepsilon$-accurate on the family for $f^-=g+\phi^-(\langle\theta,z\rangle)$;
\item[(iii)] for every $p\in[-1,1]^d$, every $\tau\ge0$ and each $\mathcal{Q}\in\{\mathcal{I}^{\mathrm{ind}},\mathcal{I}^{\mathrm{joint}},\mathcal{I}^{\mathrm{cand}}\}$,
\[
 \mathcal{Q}_{D_p}\big(X^{A^-,\phi^-}+\tau G\big)=\mathcal{Q}_{D_{-p}}\big(X^{A,\phi}+\tau G\big),
\]
so the suprema of the two sides over $p$ agree.
\end{enumerate}
Consequently, the two-sided bound \eqref{eq:main} of Theorem~\ref{thm:main}, and its form for the
infimum over any nonempty class of accurate learners, hold for $\phi$ with the same threshold, the same
conditions on $n$ and $d$ and the same constants, evaluated at $b=\phi'(0)$. So does the prior-averaged
lower bound in its finite form
$M^2\le2\ln2\,(V+n\tau^2)\,\mathbb{E}_\Pi\mathcal{Q}_{D_p}(X^{A,\phi}+\tau G)$, with the budgets $M,V$ of
Proposition~\ref{prop:finite} (when $M>0$) and the same prior $\Pi_\kappa$. Together with the
zero-slope example of Section~\ref{sec:necessity}, where accuracy forces no information, this shows
that the slope condition of Assumption~\ref{ass:class} may be read as $b=|\phi'(0)|>0$.

name: Reflection

title: Proof
body_md:
(i) On the symmetric neighbourhood of $[-1,1]$, $\phi^-$ is convex and $C^2$, as the composition of
$\phi$ with $t\mapsto-t$. Moreover $(\phi^-)'(t)=-\phi'(-t)$ and $(\phi^-)''(t)=\phi''(-t)$, so
$-(\phi^-)'(0)=\phi'(0)=b$, $|(\phi^-)'|\le L$ and $0\le(\phi^-)''\le H$ on $[-1,1]$.

(ii) Negation maps $\mathcal Z$ onto itself and $D_p$ to $D_{-p}$, because
$\mathbb{P}(-\sqrt dZ_k=1)=(1-p_k)/2$ and the coordinates stay independent. Write
$F^\phi_D(\theta)=\mathbb{E}_D[g(\theta)+\phi(\langle\theta,Z\rangle)]$, and $F^{\phi^-}_D$ likewise. Since
$\phi^-(\langle\theta,z\rangle)=\phi(\langle\theta,-z\rangle)$, we have $F^{\phi^-}_{D_p}=F^\phi_{D_{-p}}$ on $W$. Negating
every point of an i.i.d.\ sample from $D_p$ gives an i.i.d.\ sample from $D_{-p}$, independent of $R$.
So, for every $\theta\in W$,
\[
 \mathbb{E}_{S_n\sim D_p^n,R}\,F^{\phi^-}_{D_p}\big(A_n^-(S_n;R)\big)
 =\mathbb{E}_{S_n\sim D_{-p}^n,R}\,F^\phi_{D_{-p}}\big(A_n(S_n;R)\big)
 \le F^\phi_{D_{-p}}(\theta)+\varepsilon=F^{\phi^-}_{D_p}(\theta)+\varepsilon,
\]
by the accuracy of $A_n$ at $D_{-p}$, as $-p\in[-1,1]^d$. Properness and measurability are inherited
from $A_n$.

(iii) On the supersample, consider the map that negates each of the $2n$ candidates and keeps the
selection bits $U$, the seed $R$ and the noise $G$. It is a measurable involution, and it carries the
joint law of $(\widetilde Z,U,R,G)$ under $D_p$ to that under $D_{-p}$. It negates the training set, so the
output of $A_n^-$ at an outcome is the output $\widehat\theta$ of $A_n$ at the image outcome, and
$X^{A^-,\phi^-}_i=\phi(\langle\widehat\theta,-Z_{1,i}\rangle)-\phi(\langle\widehat\theta,-Z_{0,i}\rangle)$ is the value of $X^{A,\phi}_i$ at
the image outcome, whose candidates are the $-Z_{j,i}$. Hence $(X^{A^-,\phi^-}+\tau G,U)$ under $D_p$
has the law of $(X^{A,\phi}+\tau G,U)$ under $D_{-p}$, which proves (iii) for $\mathcal{I}^{\mathrm{ind}}$ and $\mathcal{I}^{\mathrm{joint}}$; and
$(X^{A^-,\phi^-}+\tau G,U,\widetilde Z)$ under $D_p$ has the law of $(X^{A,\phi}+\tau G,U,-\widetilde Z)$ under $D_{-p}$.
Mutual information does not change when one argument is replaced by its image under a measurable
bijection with measurable inverse, and $I(Y;U\mid\widetilde Z)=I(U;(Y,\widetilde Z))-I(U;\widetilde Z)$, so (iii) holds for
$\mathcal{I}^{\mathrm{cand}}$ as well. Since $p\mapsto-p$ is a bijection of $[-1,1]^d$, the suprema agree.

It remains to prove the consequence. The prior $\Pi_\kappa$ has independent coordinates with the even
density $\pi_\kappa$, so it is invariant under $p\mapsto-p$, and averaging (iii) over $\Pi_\kappa$
shows that the prior averages for $(A^-,\phi^-)$ and $(A,\phi)$ coincide. Apply Theorem~\ref{thm:main} and the
finite prior-averaged bound to the link $\phi^-$, which is admissible by (i), and to the learner
$A_n^-$, which is $\varepsilon$-accurate on the family by (ii); for the infimum over a nonempty class of
learners that are accurate for $\phi$, apply them to the class of the reflected learners $A_n^-$.

name: Without a regularizer

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $\widehat\theta$ be a proper learner that is $\varepsilon$-accurate on the family. Here
$F_p(\theta)=\mathbb{E}_p\phi(\langle\theta,Z\rangle)$, which is continuous on the compact set $W$, so its minimum over
$W$ exists. In this proof,
\[
 v=\frac{4\varepsilon^2}{b^2},\qquad \kappa=v^{-1}-1=\frac{b^2}{4\varepsilon^2}-1,
\]
and $\Pi=\Pi_\kappa$ is the beta prior of Appendix~\ref{app:prior-moments} with this $\kappa$, so that
$\mathbb{E}\lVert\mu_p\rVert^2=v$. As $\varepsilon\le b/4$, we have $v\le1/4$, so
$\kappa=(1-v)/v\ge3/(4v)\ge b^2/(8\varepsilon^2)>0$. The conditions on $d$ give $dv=4d\varepsilon^2/b^2\ge128$,
$1/d\le\varepsilon^2/(32b^2)$ and $\rho=n/d\le1/32$; so the constant $K_0=K_0(\rho)$ of
Appendix~\ref{app:tails} satisfies $K_0\le K_0^*<2.031$. Finally,
$\varepsilon\le b^3/(64(H+1)(b+\sqrt{c_+}))\le b^2/(64(H+1))$.

\emph{Calibration.} Fix $p$ and write $\mu=\mu_p$. Let $\theta_c=\mu/\lVert\mu\rVert$ if $\mu\ne0$ and
$\theta_c=0$ if $\mu=0$, so that $\theta_c\in W$ and $\langle\theta_c,\mu\rangle=\lVert\mu\rVert$. The link remainder
$u(t)=\phi(t)-\phi(0)+bt$ satisfies $0\le u(t)\le Ht^2/2$ on $[-1,1]$ (see the opening of
Appendix~\ref{app:mainproof}). Together with \eqref{eq:margin-variance} and $\lVert\theta_c\rVert\le1$, this
gives
\[
 F_p(\theta_c)=\phi(0)-b\lVert\mu\rVert+\mathbb{E}_p\,u(\langle\theta_c,Z\rangle)
 \le\phi(0)-b\lVert\mu\rVert+\frac H2\Big(\lVert\mu\rVert^2+\frac1d\Big),
\]
while $u\ge0$ gives $F_p(\theta)\ge\phi(0)-b\langle\theta,\mu\rangle$ for every $\theta\in W$. Accuracy at $D_p$
therefore gives $\phi(0)-b\,\mathbb{E}_p\langle\widehat\theta,\mu\rangle\le\mathbb{E}_pF_p(\widehat\theta)\le F_p(\theta_c)+\varepsilon$, that is,
\[
 b\,\mathbb{E}_p\langle\widehat\theta,\mu\rangle\ge b\lVert\mu\rVert-\varepsilon-\frac H2\Big(\lVert\mu\rVert^2+\frac1d\Big).
\]
Unlike in Appendix~\ref{app:calibration}, the comparator is the unit vector along $\mu_p$, and no
growth condition is used. Now average over $p\sim\Pi$. By \eqref{eq:prior-low} with $q=1$,
$\mathbb{E}\lVert\mu_p\rVert\ge\sqrt v\,(1+1/(dv))^{-1/2}$, and $\mathbb{E}\lVert\mu_p\rVert^2=v$ by \eqref{eq:prior-moments}, so
\[
 b\,\mathbb{E}_\Pi\langle\widehat\theta,\mu_p\rangle\ \ge\ \widetilde A:=b\sqrt v\Big(1+\frac1{dv}\Big)^{-1/2}-\varepsilon
 -\frac H2\Big(v+\frac1d\Big).
\]
Here $b\sqrt v=2\varepsilon$ and $(1+1/(dv))^{1/2}\le(129/128)^{1/2}\le8/7$, so the first term is at least
$7\varepsilon/4$; and $v+1/d\le5\varepsilon^2/b^2$ and $\varepsilon\le b^2/(64(H+1))$ give
$(H/2)(v+1/d)\le5H\varepsilon^2/(2b^2)\le\varepsilon/4$. Hence $\widetilde A\ge\varepsilon/2$.

\emph{Signed mean.} The derivation of \eqref{eq:taylor-main} in Appendix~\ref{app:signed} uses only
the link conditions, properness and Lemma~\ref{lem:fp}, so it applies here: with $m=\langle\widehat\theta,\mu_p\rangle$ and
$s_i=\langle\widehat\theta,Z^{\mathrm{tr}}_i-\mu_p\rangle$,
\[
 \sum_i\mathbb{E}_\Pi\sigma_iX_i\ge b\kappa\,\mathbb{E}_\Pi m-\mathbb{E}_\Pi\Big[u'(m)\sum_is_i\Big]
 -\frac H2\,\mathbb{E}_\Pi\lVertB_{\mathrm{tr}}\widehat\theta\rVert^2 .
\]
The first term is at least $\kappa\widetilde A$. Without localization, properness bounds the other two.
Pointwise, $|u'(m)|\le H|m|\le H\lVert\mu_p\rVert$ and
$|\sum_is_i|=|\langle\widehat\theta,\sum_i(Z^{\mathrm{tr}}_i-\mu_p)\rangle|\le\lVert\sum_i(Z^{\mathrm{tr}}_i-\mu_p)\rVert$, and given $p$ the centred
training sum has second moment $n(1-\lVert\mu_p\rVert^2)\le n$ (Appendix~\ref{app:sample-lower}). The
Cauchy--Schwarz inequality therefore gives
\[
 \mathbb{E}_\Pi\Big|u'(m)\sum_is_i\Big|
 \le H\Big(\mathbb{E}\lVert\mu_p\rVert^2\;\mathbb{E}_\Pi\Big\|\sum_i(Z^{\mathrm{tr}}_i-\mu_p)\Big\|^2\Big)^{1/2}\le H\sqrt{nv}.
\]
Also $\lVertB_{\mathrm{tr}}\widehat\theta\rVert^2\le\lVertB_{\mathrm{tr}}\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}^2$, and $\mathbb{E}_p\lVertB_{\mathrm{tr}}\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}^2\le K_0$ at every $p$
(Appendix~\ref{app:tails}). Therefore
\[
 \sum_i\mathbb{E}_\Pi\sigma_iX_i\ \ge\ M:=\kappa\widetilde A-H\sqrt{nv}-\frac H2K_0 .
\]
With $\kappa\ge b^2/(8\varepsilon^2)$, $\widetilde A\ge\varepsilon/2$, $\sqrt{nv}=2\sqrt{n\varepsilon^2}/b\le2\sqrt{c_+}/b$ and
$K_0<4$,
\[
 M\ \ge\ \frac{b^2}{16\varepsilon}-H\Big(\frac{2\sqrt{c_+}}b+2\Big)
 \ \ge\ \frac{b^2}{16\varepsilon}-\frac{b^2}{32\varepsilon}\ =\ \frac{b^2}{32\varepsilon},
\]
because $\varepsilon\le b^3/(64(H+1)(b+\sqrt{c_+}))$ is equivalent to $(H+1)(2\sqrt{c_+}/b+2)\le b^2/(32\varepsilon)$.

\emph{Energy.} The derivation of \eqref{eq:energy} in Appendix~\ref{app:energy} uses only the link
conditions and properness. With $\lVert\widehat\theta\rVert\le1$ and $\mathbb{E}_p\lVertB_{\mathrm{tr}}\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}^2\le K_0$, it gives, at every $p$,
\[
 \mathbb{E}_p\lVertX\rVert^2=\sum_i\mathbb{E}_pX_i^2\ \le\ V:=L^2(K_0+\rho)\ \le\ 3L^2,
\]
since $K_0+\rho<2.031+1/32<3$.

\emph{The two bounds.} The prior $\Pi$ depends only on $b$ and $\varepsilon$, so it is fixed before the
learner, and $p$ is drawn independently of the selection bits, the seed and the noise. The energy
bound at every $p$ gives $\sum_i\mathbb{E}_\Pi X_i^2\le V$, and $M>0$. So the lower bound \eqref{eq:lower} of
Theorem~\ref{thm:transfer} gives, for every $\tau\ge0$,
\[
 \mathbb{E}_\Pi\mathcal{I}^{\mathrm{ind}}_{D_p}(X+\tau G)\ \ge\ \frac{M^2}{2\ln2\,(V+n\tau^2)}
 \ \ge\ \frac{b^4/(1024\varepsilon^2)}{2\ln2\,(3L^2+c_+\tau^2/\varepsilon^2)}
 \ =\ \frac{b^4}{2048\ln2\,(3L^2\varepsilon^2+c_+\tau^2)}\ \ge\ \frac c{\varepsilon^2+\tau^2},
\]
by $n\le c_+\varepsilon^{-2}$ and $3L^2\varepsilon^2+c_+\tau^2\le\max\{3L^2,c_+\}(\varepsilon^2+\tau^2)$. By
\eqref{eq:hierarchy} the same bound holds for $\mathcal{I}^{\mathrm{joint}}$ and $\mathcal{I}^{\mathrm{cand}}$, and a prior average is at most the
supremum over $p$.

For the upper bound, fix $p$ and apply Theorem~\ref{thm:transfer}(b) with the reference $x_p(\widetilde Z)=0$
and $V_{\mathrm{res}}=V$. It gives $\mathcal{I}^{\mathrm{cand}}_{D_p}(X+\tau G)\le n$ for every $\tau\ge0$ and, for $\tau>0$, by
$\ln(1+y)\le y$,
\[
 \mathcal{I}^{\mathrm{cand}}_{D_p}(X+\tau G)\le\frac n{2\ln2}\ln\Big(1+\frac V{n\tau^2}\Big)\le\frac V{2\ln2\,\tau^2}
 \le\frac{3L^2}{2\ln2\,\tau^2}.
\]
Hence $(\varepsilon^2+\tau^2)\,\mathcal{I}^{\mathrm{cand}}_{D_p}(X+\tau G)\le n\varepsilon^2+3L^2/(2\ln2)\le c_++3L^2/(2\ln2)$, where the
second term is not needed at $\tau=0$. By \eqref{eq:hierarchy} the same bound holds for $\mathcal{I}^{\mathrm{ind}}$ and
$\mathcal{I}^{\mathrm{joint}}$, at every $p$, and therefore for the supremum over $p$.

title: Definitions
body_md:
Recall from Section~\ref{sec:consequences} that a learner
$\widehat\theta=A_n(S_n;R)$ is $(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{DP}},\delta)$-differentially private if for all training sets
$S,S'\in\mathcal Z^n$ that differ in one point and every measurable $E\subseteq W$,
\[
 \mathbb{P}\big(A_n(S;R)\in E\big)\le e^{\varepsilon_{\mathrm{DP}}}\,\mathbb{P}\big(A_n(S';R)\in E\big)+\delta ;
\]
this is privacy for the replacement of one training point. Write
$K_\phi=\sup_{s,t\in[-1,1]}|\phi(s)-\phi(t)|$ for the oscillation of the link on the margin interval.
Under Assumption~\ref{ass:class}, the mean value theorem gives $K_\phi\le2L$. Since $\lVert\widehat\theta\rVert\le1$
and $\lVertZ\rVert\le1$, every loss difference satisfies $|X_i|\le K_\phi$.

label: lem:dp-forms
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:dp-forms}
Let $\theta$ and $\theta'$ be random elements of $W$ with
$\mathbb{P}(\theta\in E)\le e^{\varepsilon_{\mathrm{DP}}}\,\mathbb{P}(\theta'\in E)+\delta$ for every measurable $E\subseteq W$, where
$\varepsilon_{\mathrm{DP}}\ge0$, and let $c>0$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(a)] Every measurable $\Psi:W\to[0,c]$ satisfies $\mathbb{E}\Psi(\theta)\le e^{\varepsilon_{\mathrm{DP}}}\,\mathbb{E}\Psi(\theta')+\delta c$.
\item[(b)] If the hypothesis also holds with $\theta$ and $\theta'$ exchanged, every measurable
$\Xi:W\to[-c,c]$ satisfies
$\mathbb{E}\Xi(\theta)-\mathbb{E}\Xi(\theta')\le(e^{\varepsilon_{\mathrm{DP}}}-1)\big(\mathbb{E}|\Xi(\theta)|+\mathbb{E}|\Xi(\theta')|\big)+2\delta c$.
\item[(c)] Under the same two-sided hypothesis, every measurable test $\psi:W\to[0,1]$ satisfies
$\mathbb{E}\psi(\theta)-\mathbb{E}\psi(\theta')\le(e^{\varepsilon_{\mathrm{DP}}}-1+2\delta)/(e^{\varepsilon_{\mathrm{DP}}}+1)$.
\end{enumerate}

name: Two-point forms of differential privacy

title: Proof
body_md:
(a) By the layer-cake formula and the hypothesis applied to the measurable sets
$E_t=\{\Psi\ge t\}$,
\[
 \mathbb{E}\Psi(\theta)=\int_0^c\mathbb{P}\big(\Psi(\theta)\ge t\big)\,dt
 \le\int_0^c\Big(e^{\varepsilon_{\mathrm{DP}}}\,\mathbb{P}\big(\Psi(\theta')\ge t\big)+\delta\Big)\,dt
 =e^{\varepsilon_{\mathrm{DP}}}\,\mathbb{E}\Psi(\theta')+\delta c .
\]
(b) Write $\Xi=\Xi^+-\Xi^-$ with $0\le\Xi^\pm\le|\Xi|\le c$. Part~(a) for $\Xi^+$, from $\theta$ to
$\theta'$, and for $\Xi^-$, from $\theta'$ to $\theta$, gives
$\mathbb{E}\Xi^+(\theta)-\mathbb{E}\Xi^+(\theta')\le(e^{\varepsilon_{\mathrm{DP}}}-1)\,\mathbb{E}\Xi^+(\theta')+\delta c$ and
$\mathbb{E}\Xi^-(\theta')-\mathbb{E}\Xi^-(\theta)\le(e^{\varepsilon_{\mathrm{DP}}}-1)\,\mathbb{E}\Xi^-(\theta)+\delta c$. Add the two, and use
$\Xi^+(\theta')\le|\Xi(\theta')|$, $\Xi^-(\theta)\le|\Xi(\theta)|$ and $e^{\varepsilon_{\mathrm{DP}}}-1\ge0$.
(c) With $x=\mathbb{E}\psi(\theta)$ and $y=\mathbb{E}\psi(\theta')$, part~(a) for $\psi$, and in the reverse direction
for $1-\psi$, gives $x\le e^{\varepsilon_{\mathrm{DP}}}y+\delta$ and $1-y\le e^{\varepsilon_{\mathrm{DP}}}(1-x)+\delta$. Adding them gives
$(1+e^{\varepsilon_{\mathrm{DP}}})(x-y)\le e^{\varepsilon_{\mathrm{DP}}}-1+2\delta$.

label: prop:dp-pair
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:dp-pair}
Let $D$ be a law of $Z$ carried by a set $\mathcal S$ of points with norm at most $1$ (for the family,
$\mathcal S=\mathcal Z$), let $\phi$ be measurable on $[-1,1]$ with $K_\phi<\infty$, and let $A_n$ be a
measurable proper learner that satisfies the privacy inequality, with $\varepsilon_{\mathrm{DP}}\ge0$, for all training
sets in $\mathcal S^n$ that differ in one point. On the supersample under $D$, every pair $i$
satisfies
\[
 \mathbb{E}\,\sigma_iX_i\le(e^{\varepsilon_{\mathrm{DP}}}-1)\,\mathbb{E}|X_i|+K_\phi\delta .
\]
No accuracy is assumed.
head: environment
name: Privacy caps the signed loss difference of every pair

title: Proof
body_md:
Fix $\widetilde Z=\tilde z$ with all candidates in $\mathcal S$, which is an event of probability one, and fix
the other selection bits $U_{-i}$. The two values of $U_i$ select training sets $S^0,S^1\in\mathcal S^n$
that differ only in position $i$, so the laws of $A_n(S^0;R)$ and $A_n(S^1;R)$ satisfy the privacy
inequality in both directions. Given $\tilde z$, $X_i=\Phi_{\tilde z}(\widehat\theta)_i$, where
$\Phi_{\tilde z}(\theta)_i=\phi(\langle\theta,z_{1,i}\rangle)-\phi(\langle\theta,z_{0,i}\rangle)$ is the release map, and
$|\Phi_{\tilde z}(\cdot)_i|\le K_\phi$ on $W$. The bit $U_i$ is fair and independent of
$(\widetilde Z,U_{-i},R)$, and $\sigma_i=1$ exactly when $U_i=0$. So Lemma~\ref{lem:dp-forms}(b) with
$c=K_\phi$ gives
\[
 \mathbb{E}[\sigma_iX_i\mid\widetilde Z,U_{-i}]
 =\tfrac12\Big(\mathbb{E}\,\Phi_{\tilde z}\big(A_n(S^0;R)\big)_i-\mathbb{E}\,\Phi_{\tilde z}\big(A_n(S^1;R)\big)_i\Big)
 \le(e^{\varepsilon_{\mathrm{DP}}}-1)\,\mathbb{E}\big[|X_i|\bigm|\widetilde Z,U_{-i}\big]+K_\phi\delta .
\]
Integrating over $(\widetilde Z,U_{-i})$ proves the claim.

label: cor:dp-audit
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{cor:dp-audit}
Let $\phi$ satisfy the link conditions of Assumption~\ref{ass:class}, let $A_n$ be a measurable proper
$(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{DP}},\delta)$-differentially private learner with $\varepsilon_{\mathrm{DP}}\ge0$, and let $\kappa>0$, $M>0$ and $V$
satisfy $\mathbb{E}_\Pi\sum_i\mathbb{E}_p\sigma_iX_i\ge M$ and $\mathbb{E}_\Pi\sum_i\mathbb{E}_pX_i^2\le V$ for the beta prior
$\Pi_\kappa$, as in the finite form of Proposition~\ref{prop:finite}. Then, for every $t>0$,
\[
 M\le(e^{\varepsilon_{\mathrm{DP}}}-1)\,\frac{V/t+nt}2+nK_\phi\delta ,
\]
and hence, for every $\varepsilon>0$ and with $\bar M=M/(n\varepsilon)$ and $\bar V=V/(n\varepsilon^2)>0$,
\[
 \bar M\le(e^{\varepsilon_{\mathrm{DP}}}-1)\sqrt{\bar V}+\frac{K_\phi\delta}\varepsilon .
\]
head: environment
name: Privacy caps the audit statistic

title: Proof
body_md:
For every $p\in[-1,1]^d$ the law $D_p$ is carried by $\mathcal Z$, whose points have norm $1$. So
Proposition~\ref{prop:dp-pair} and $|x|\le x^2/(2t)+t/2$ give
$\sum_i\mathbb{E}_p\sigma_iX_i\le(e^{\varepsilon_{\mathrm{DP}}}-1)\big(\sum_i\mathbb{E}_pX_i^2/t+nt\big)/2+nK_\phi\delta$. Average over the
prior, which is carried by $[-1,1]^d$, and use the two budget bounds and $e^{\varepsilon_{\mathrm{DP}}}-1\ge0$. For the
second form take $t=\varepsilon\sqrt{\bar V}$, so that $V/t=nt=n\varepsilon\sqrt{\bar V}$, and divide by $n\varepsilon$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $\widehat\theta=A_n(S_n;R)$ be $\varepsilon$-accurate on the family and $(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{DP}},\delta)$-differentially private
with $\varepsilon_{\mathrm{DP}}\ge0$, in the regime of Theorem~\ref{thm:main}. Let $M$ and $V$ be the budgets of the
finite form of Proposition~\ref{prop:finite} at the actual $n$, $d$ and $\varepsilon$, and $\bar M=M/(n\varepsilon)$,
$\bar V=V/(n\varepsilon^2)$. By Appendix~\ref{app:orders}, $M\ge c_Mn\varepsilon>0$ and $V\le C_Vn\varepsilon^2$, and
$V>0$ because $L\ge b>0$ and $V=L^2(C_\theta+\rho w_\theta)$ with $\rho w_\theta>0$.
Corollary~\ref{cor:dp-audit} gives the finite bound
\[
 e^{\varepsilon_{\mathrm{DP}}}-1\ \ge\ \frac{\bar M-K_\phi\delta/\varepsilon}{\sqrt{\bar V}} ,
\]
in which $\bar M\ge c_M$ and $\bar V\le C_V$. For the order form, take $t=\varepsilon\sqrt{\max\{C_V,1\}}$ in
Corollary~\ref{cor:dp-audit}: then $V/t\le n\varepsilon\sqrt{\max\{C_V,1\}}=nt$, so
\[
 c_Mn\varepsilon\le M\le(e^{\varepsilon_{\mathrm{DP}}}-1)\,n\varepsilon\sqrt{\max\{C_V,1\}}+nK_\phi\delta .
\]
Dividing by $n\varepsilon\sqrt{\max\{C_V,1\}}\ge n\varepsilon$ and using $\delta\ge0$ and $K_\phi\le2L$,
\[
 e^{\varepsilon_{\mathrm{DP}}}-1\ \ge\ c'-\frac{K_\phi\delta}\varepsilon\ \ge\ c'-\frac{2L\delta}\varepsilon,\qquad
 c'=\frac{c_M}{\sqrt{\max\{C_V,1\}}}=\sqrt{2\ln2\,c_1},
\]
where $c_1=c_M^2/(2\ln2\max\{C_V,1\})$ is the lower constant of Theorem~\ref{thm:main}. This proves
Corollary~\ref{cor:consequences}(ii). In particular, if $4L\delta\le c'\varepsilon$ then
$e^{\varepsilon_{\mathrm{DP}}}-1\ge c'/2$, that is, $\varepsilon_{\mathrm{DP}}\ge\ln(1+c'/2)$: in the regime of Theorem~\ref{thm:main},
accuracy forces $\varepsilon_{\mathrm{DP}}=\Omega(1)$ unless $\delta=\Omega(\varepsilon)$. Since $n\ge c_-\varepsilon^{-2/q}$ and
$q\le2$ give $\varepsilon\ge(c_-/n)^{q/2}\ge\min\{1,c_-\}/n$, the usual requirement $\delta=o(1/n)$ makes the
$\delta$-term negligible.

label: lem:powerlinear
title: Lemma
head: environment
name: Every-learner lower bound for power-linear losses

title: Proof
body_md:
The argument is the one of Section~\ref{sec:moments}, and it is shorter because the link is affine:
the train--ghost remainder of Step~3 vanishes.

\emph{Population minimizer.} For $p\in[-1,1]^d$, the population risk is
$F_p(\theta)=\lVert\theta\rVert^r/r-\langle\theta,\mu_p\rangle$ on $W$. Young's inequality,
$\langle\theta,\mu_p\rangle\le\lVert\theta\rVert\lVert\mu_p\rVert\le\lVert\theta\rVert^r/r+\lVert\mu_p\rVert^q/q$, gives
$F_p\ge-\lVert\mu_p\rVert^q/q$, with equality at $\theta_p^*=\lVert\mu_p\rVert^{q-2}\mu_p$ ($\theta_p^*=0$ when
$\mu_p=0$). This point lies in $W$ because $\lVert\theta_p^*\rVert=\lVert\mu_p\rVert^{q-1}\le1$. Hence
\[
 \min_WF_p=-\lVert\mu_p\rVert^q/q,\qquad \lVert\theta_p^*\rVert=\lVert\mu_p\rVert^{q-1}.
\]

\emph{Calibration.} As $\lVert\widehat\theta\rVert^r/r\ge0$, we have $F_p(\widehat\theta)\ge-\langle\widehat\theta,\mu_p\rangle$, so accuracy at $D_p$
gives $\mathbb{E}_p\langle\widehat\theta,\mu_p\rangle\ge-\mathbb{E}_pF_p(\widehat\theta)\ge\lVert\mu_p\rVert^q/q-\varepsilon$. Averaging over the prior and
using \eqref{eq:prior-low},
\[
 \mathbb{E}_\Pi\langle\widehat\theta,\mu_p\rangle\ \ge\ \frac1q\,\mathbb{E}\lVert\mu_p\rVert^q-\varepsilon\ \ge\ \widetilde A .
\]

\emph{Signed mean.} For the affine link, $\sigma_iX_i=\langle\widehat\theta,Z^{\mathrm{tr}}_i-Z^{\mathrm{gh}}_i\rangle$. Conditionally on $p$,
the training set and the seed, each ghost is a fresh draw from $D_p$ that is independent of $\widehat\theta$,
so $\mathbb{E}_\Pi\langle\widehat\theta,Z^{\mathrm{gh}}_i-\mu_p\rangle=0$. Lemma~\ref{lem:fp} and the calibration therefore give, since
$\kappa>0$,
\[
 \sum_i\mathbb{E}_\Pi\sigma_iX_i=\mathbb{E}_\Pi\Big\langle\widehat\theta,\sum_i(Z^{\mathrm{tr}}_i-\mu_p)\Big\rangle
 =\kappa\,\mathbb{E}_\Pi\langle\widehat\theta,\mu_p\rangle\ \ge\ \kappa\widetilde A=\widetilde M .
\]

\emph{Localization.} Let $e=\widehat\theta-\theta_p^*$. Since $F_p-g$ is linear,
$F_p(\theta)-F_p(\theta_p^*)-\langle\nabla F_p(\theta_p^*),\theta-\theta_p^*\rangle=D_g(\theta,\theta_p^*)$, and
the first-order condition for the minimizer on $W$ makes the inner product nonnegative for
$\theta\in W$. So $F_p(\theta)-\min_WF_p\ge D_g(\theta,\theta_p^*)\ge a_-\lVert\theta-\theta_p^*\rVert^r$ on
$W$. Accuracy and Jensen's inequality ($r\ge2$) give
$\mathbb{E}_p\lVerte\rVert^2\le(\mathbb{E}_p\lVerte\rVert^r)^{2/r}\le(\varepsilon/a_-)^{2/r}$, and $\lVerte\rVert\le2$ gives $\mathbb{E}_p\lVerte\rVert^2\le4$;
so $\mathbb{E}_p\lVerte\rVert^2\le w$ at every $p$. Minkowski's inequality, the formula for
$\lVert\theta_p^*\rVert$ and \eqref{eq:prior-concave} give
\[
 \big(\mathbb{E}_\Pi\lVert\widehat\theta\rVert^2\big)^{1/2}\le\big(\mathbb{E}_\Pi\lVerte\rVert^2\big)^{1/2}
 +\big(\mathbb{E}\lVert\mu_p\rVert^{2(q-1)}\big)^{1/2}\le\sqrt w+v^{(q-1)/2},
\]
and together with $\lVert\widehat\theta\rVert\le1$ this is $\mathbb{E}_\Pi\lVert\widehat\theta\rVert^2\le w_\theta$.

\emph{Energy.} Write $s_i=\langle\widehat\theta,Z^{\mathrm{tr}}_i-\mu_p\rangle$ and $s_i^{\mathrm{gh}}=\langle\widehat\theta,Z^{\mathrm{gh}}_i-\mu_p\rangle$, so that
$X_i^2=(s_i-s_i^{\mathrm{gh}})^2$. Conditionally on $p$, the training set and the seed,
$s_i^{\mathrm{gh}}$ has mean zero, and its second moment is at most $\lVert\widehat\theta\rVert^2/d$, because the
covariance of $D_p$ is diagonal with entries $(1-p_k^2)/d\le1/d$. The cross terms therefore vanish,
and
\[
 \sum_i\mathbb{E}_pX_i^2=\mathbb{E}_p\lVertB_{\mathrm{tr}}\widehat\theta\rVert^2+\sum_i\mathbb{E}_p(s_i^{\mathrm{gh}})^2
 \le\mathbb{E}_p\big[\lVertB_{\mathrm{tr}}\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}^2\lVert\widehat\theta\rVert^2\big]+\frac nd\,\mathbb{E}_p\lVert\widehat\theta\rVert^2 .
\]
By Lemma~\ref{lem:matrix}, in the form proved in Appendix~\ref{app:tails} for all $n$ and $d$,
$\mathbb{P}_p(\lVertB_{\mathrm{tr}}\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}^2>K_0+K_1t)\le e^{-t}$ for $t\ge0$ at every $p$, hence also under the prior.
Lemma~\ref{lem:weighted}, applied with the weight $\lVert\widehat\theta\rVert^2\le1$ and
$\mathbb{E}_\Pi\lVert\widehat\theta\rVert^2\le w_\theta\le1$, gives
$\mathbb{E}_\Pi[\lVertB_{\mathrm{tr}}\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}^2\lVert\widehat\theta\rVert^2]\le\mathfrak{T}_1(w_\theta;K_0,K_1)$. Hence
$\sum_i\mathbb{E}_\Pi X_i^2\le\widetilde V$.

\emph{Transfer.} The prior $\Pi_\kappa$ depends only on $r$ and $\varepsilon$, so it is fixed before the
learner, and the selection bits are independent of $p$. The lower bound \eqref{eq:lower} of
Theorem~\ref{thm:transfer}, whose proof in Appendix~\ref{app:fairbit} uses only the signed mean and
the energy, applies with $M=\widetilde M>0$ and $V=\widetilde V$. This is
\eqref{eq:powerlinear-information} for $\mathcal{I}^{\mathrm{ind}}$. The chain \eqref{eq:hierarchy} at every $p$ gives it
for $\mathcal{I}^{\mathrm{joint}}$ and $\mathcal{I}^{\mathrm{cand}}$.

title: Proof
body_md:
\emph{The regularizer.} On $W$, $D_g(\theta',\theta)=\lVert\theta'-\theta\rVert^2/2$, and
$\lVert\theta'-\theta\rVert\le2$ gives $\lVert\theta'-\theta\rVert^2/2\ge\lVert\theta'-\theta\rVert^4/8$. The bound
$\lVert\theta\rVert^2/2\le a_+\lVert\theta\rVert^4$ fails whenever $0<\lVert\theta\rVert^2<1/(2a_+)$. So $g$ has lower
curvature of power $4$, but growth of power $2$ only; $f_2$ satisfies Assumption~\ref{ass:class} with
$r=2$ and $a_-=a_+=1/2$, and not with $r=4$.

\emph{Accuracy of the mean learner.} Let $D$ be a law on the unit ball, with mean $\mu_D$. For $f_2$,
$F_D(\theta)=\lVert\theta-\mu_D\rVert^2/2-\lVert\mu_D\rVert^2/2$, which is minimized on $W$ at $\mu_D$. The mean
$\bar Z$ lies in $W$, and its expected excess risk is
$\mathbb{E}\lVert\bar Z-\mu_D\rVert^2/2=(\mathbb{E}\lVertZ\rVert^2-\lVert\mu_D\rVert^2)/(2n)\le1/(2n)$. As $1/(2n)\le n^{-2/3}$ for
$n\ge1$, the mean learner is itself $\varepsilon$-accurate on the family.

\emph{Upper bound for the mean learner.} We prove more than the proposition needs: for $n\ge16$,
$d\ge32n$, every $p$ and every $\tau>0$,
\begin{equation*}
 \mathcal{I}^{\mathrm{cand}}_{D_p}(X^{(2)}+\tau G)\le\frac{2K_0+2K_1[1+\ln(4n)]}{2\ln2\;n\tau^2}\le\frac3{n\tau^2}.
\end{equation*}
Proposition~\ref{prop:separation}(iii) states the same bound. Fix $p$. For $f_2$ the population minimizer is
$\theta_p^*=\mu_p$, so the reference of Proposition~\ref{prop:finite} is $X_p^*(\widetilde Z)=-\Delta\mu_p$,
which depends only on $p$ and the candidates, and $X^{(2)}-X_p^*(\widetilde Z)=-\Delta(\bar Z-\mu_p)$. At
$D_p$, $\mathbb{E}_p\lVert\bar Z-\mu_p\rVert^2=(1-\lVert\mu_p\rVert^2)/n\le1/n$ and $\lVert\bar Z-\mu_p\rVert^2\le4$. By
Lemma~\ref{lem:matrix}, $\mathbb{P}_p(\lVert\Delta\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}^2>2K_0+2K_1t)\le e^{-t}$ for $t\ge0$. The mean $\bar Z$
depends on the candidates in $\Delta$, and Lemma~\ref{lem:weighted} allows this dependence: with the
weight $\lVert\bar Z-\mu_p\rVert^2\le4$ it gives
\[
 \mathbb{E}_p\lVertX^{(2)}-X_p^*(\widetilde Z)\rVert^2\le\mathbb{E}_p\big[\lVert\Delta\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}^2\lVert\bar Z-\mu_p\rVert^2\big]
 \le\mathfrak{T}_4(1/n;2K_0,2K_1)=\frac1n\big\{2K_0+2K_1[1+\ln(4n)]\big\}.
\]
The upper bound \eqref{eq:upper} of Theorem~\ref{thm:transfer}, which at a given law uses only the
residual bound at that law (Appendix~\ref{app:hierarchy}), and $\ln(1+x)\le x$ give the first
inequality of the display. For $d\ge32n$, $2K_0\le2K_0^*<4.062$ and $2K_1=4/(c_{\mathrm{net}} d)\le0.282/n$;
since $(1+\ln4n)/n$ decreases in $n$, the numerator is at most $4.062+0.282\cdot(1+\ln64)/16<4.153$
for $n\ge16$, and $4.153/(2\ln2)<3$. At $\tau=\varepsilon=n^{-2/3}$ we have $n\tau^2=n^{-1/3}$, so the bound
is $3n^{1/3}$ at every $p$; the chain \eqref{eq:hierarchy} gives the same bound for $\mathcal{I}^{\mathrm{ind}}$ and $\mathcal{I}^{\mathrm{joint}}$.

\emph{Lower bound for every accurate learner.} Let $n\ge182$, $d\ge32n$ and $\varepsilon=n^{-2/3}$. Since
$32^{3/2}<182$, we have $\varepsilon\le1/32$. We apply Lemma~\ref{lem:powerlinear} with $r=q=2$: then $a_-=1/2$, $v=8\varepsilon\le1/4$,
$\kappa=1/(8\varepsilon)-1$, $w=2\varepsilon$ and $w_\theta=(\sqrt{2\varepsilon}+\sqrt{8\varepsilon})^2=18\varepsilon\le1$. As
$d\varepsilon\ge32n^{1/3}\ge32$, we have $dv\ge256$, and
\[
 \widetilde A=\frac{4\varepsilon}{1+1/(dv)}-\varepsilon\ge\Big(\frac{1024}{257}-1\Big)\varepsilon>2.98\,\varepsilon,\qquad
 \widetilde M=\Big(\frac1{8\varepsilon}-1\Big)\widetilde A>2.98\Big(\frac18-\frac1{32}\Big)>0.279 .
\]
Next, $n/d\le1/32$ gives $K_0\le K_0^*<2.031$, and $K_1=2/(c_{\mathrm{net}} d)\le0.141/n$. Since
$\ln(1/w_\theta)=\ln(n^{2/3}/18)$ and $(1+\ln(n^{2/3}/18))/n$ decreases for $n\ge182$,
$K_1[1+\ln(1/w_\theta)]\le0.141\cdot1.579/182<0.0013$. Hence
\[
 \widetilde V\le18\varepsilon\,\big(2.031+0.0013+\tfrac1{32}\big)<37.2\,n^{-2/3}.
\]
At $\tau=\varepsilon$, $n\tau^2=n^{-1/3}$, and Lemma~\ref{lem:powerlinear} gives, for each $\mathcal{Q}$,
\[
 \sup_p\mathcal{Q}_{D_p}(X+\varepsilon G)\ \ge\ \mathbb{E}_{p\sim\Pi_\kappa}\mathcal{Q}_{D_p}(X+\varepsilon G)
 \ \ge\ \frac{0.279^2\,n^{1/3}}{2\ln2\,(1+37.2\,n^{-1/3})}\ \ge\ 0.0074\,n^{1/3},
\]
where the last step uses $n^{-1/3}\le182^{-1/3}<0.177$.

Since the mean learner is itself $\varepsilon$-accurate, the least worst-case information over proper
$\varepsilon$-accurate learners therefore lies between $0.007\,n^{1/3}$ and $3n^{1/3}$ for each $\mathcal{Q}$.

title: Proof
body_md:
By the chain \eqref{eq:hierarchy} it suffices to treat $\mathcal{Q}=\mathcal{I}^{\mathrm{cand}}$, and $\mathcal{I}^{\mathrm{cand}}_D(Y)\le\mathrm{H}(U\mid\widetilde Z)=n$
gives the first entry of the minimum. Write $Y=X+\tau G$, and work in nats until the last step.

\emph{Lipschitz release map.} For a supersample $\tilde z=(z_{j,i})$ with every $\lVertz_{j,i}\rVert\le1$,
an event of probability one, and for $\theta\in W$, let
$\Phi_{\tilde z}(\theta)_i=\phi(\langle\theta,z_{1,i}\rangle)-\phi(\langle\theta,z_{0,i}\rangle)$, so that
$X=\Phi_{\widetilde Z}(\widehat\theta)$. For $\theta,\theta'\in W$ every margin lies in $[-1,1]$, so
$|\Phi_{\tilde z}(\theta)_i-\Phi_{\tilde z}(\theta')_i|\le L|\langle\theta-\theta',z_{1,i}\rangle|
+L|\langle\theta-\theta',z_{0,i}\rangle|\le2L\lVert\theta-\theta'\rVert$ for each $i$. Summing the squares over the
$n$ coordinates,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:dimension-lip}
 \lVert\Phi_{\tilde z}(\theta)-\Phi_{\tilde z}(\theta')\rVert\le2L\sqrt n\,\lVert\theta-\theta'\rVert
 \qquad(\theta,\theta'\in W).
\end{equation}

\emph{Net.} Put $h=\tau/(2L\sqrt n)$. If the points of a subset of $W$ are at pairwise distance at
least $h$, the open balls of radius $h/2$ around them are disjoint and lie in the ball of radius
$1+h/2$; comparing volumes, such a set has at most $(1+h/2)^d/(h/2)^d=(1+2/h)^d$ points. Let
$\mathcal T_h\subset W$ be such a set of maximal cardinality. By maximality, every $\theta\in W$ lies
within distance $h$ of some point of $\mathcal T_h$, and
\[
 |\mathcal T_h|\le(1+2/h)^d=\big(1+4L\sqrt n/\tau\big)^d .
\]
The net depends only on $d$ and $h$, not on the data or the learner.

\emph{Reference and variational bound.} Let
$\bar{\mathcal{N}}_{\tilde z}=|\mathcal T_h|^{-1}\sum_{\theta'\in\mathcal T_h}\mathcal{N}(\Phi_{\tilde z}(\theta'),\tau^2I_n)$,
a Markov kernel from supersamples to $\mathbb{R}^n$. For every such kernel, with $\operatorname{KL}$ the Kullback--Leibler
divergence,
\[
 \mathbb{E}\,\operatorname{KL}\big(P_{Y\mid U,\widetilde Z}\,\big\|\,\bar{\mathcal{N}}_{\widetilde Z}\big)
 =I(Y;U\mid\widetilde Z)+\mathbb{E}\,\operatorname{KL}\big(P_{Y\mid\widetilde Z}\,\big\|\,\bar{\mathcal{N}}_{\widetilde Z}\big)\ \ge\ I(Y;U\mid\widetilde Z).
\]
Given $(U,\widetilde Z,X)$ the observation is $Y\sim\mathcal{N}(X,\tau^2I_n)$, because $G$ is independent of the
data and of the learner. So $P_{Y\mid U,\widetilde Z}$ is the conditional average of $\mathcal{N}(X,\tau^2I_n)$
given $(U,\widetilde Z)$, and convexity of the divergence in its first argument gives
\begin{equation}\label{eq:dimension-var}
 I(Y;U\mid\widetilde Z)\le\mathbb{E}\,\operatorname{KL}\big(\mathcal{N}(X,\tau^2I_n)\,\big\|\,\bar{\mathcal{N}}_{\widetilde Z}\big).
\end{equation}

\emph{Pointwise bound.} Fix an outcome in the probability-one event above, and choose
$\theta'\in\mathcal T_h$ with $\lVert\widehat\theta-\theta'\rVert\le h$. As measures,
$\bar{\mathcal{N}}_{\tilde z}\ge|\mathcal T_h|^{-1}\mathcal{N}(\Phi_{\tilde z}(\theta'),\tau^2I_n)$, so every
probability measure $P$ satisfies
$\operatorname{KL}(P\,\|\,\bar{\mathcal{N}}_{\tilde z})\le\operatorname{KL}\big(P\,\|\,\mathcal{N}(\Phi_{\tilde z}(\theta'),\tau^2I_n)\big)
+\ln|\mathcal T_h|$. Gaussians with a common covariance satisfy
$\operatorname{KL}(\mathcal{N}(x,\tau^2I_n)\,\|\,\mathcal{N}(y,\tau^2I_n))=\lVertx-y\rVert^2/(2\tau^2)$. With
$x=X=\Phi_{\widetilde Z}(\widehat\theta)$ and $y=\Phi_{\widetilde Z}(\theta')$, \eqref{eq:dimension-lip} gives
$\lVertx-y\rVert\le2L\sqrt n\,h=\tau$, hence
\[
 \operatorname{KL}\big(\mathcal{N}(X,\tau^2I_n)\,\big\|\,\bar{\mathcal{N}}_{\widetilde Z}\big)\le\ln|\mathcal T_h|+\frac12
 \le d\ln\Big(1+\frac{4L\sqrt n}{\tau}\Big)+\frac12 .
\]
Inserting this into \eqref{eq:dimension-var} and dividing by $\ln2$ gives
$\mathcal{I}^{\mathrm{cand}}_D(Y)\le d\log_2(1+4L\sqrt n/\tau)+1/(2\ln2)$ bits. Together with the cap $n$, this is
\eqref{eq:dimension}.

\emph{Consequence.} At $\tau=\varepsilon$, \eqref{eq:dimension} bounds $\mathcal{Q}_{D_p}(X+\varepsilon G)$ at every $p$,
since every $D_p$ satisfies $\lVertZ\rVert=1$. So $cn\le d\log_2(1+4L\sqrt n/\varepsilon)+1/(2\ln2)$, and the
logarithm is positive, which gives \eqref{eq:dimension-needed}. If $n\ge c_-\varepsilon^{-2/q}$, then
$1/\varepsilon\le(n/c_-)^{q/2}$ and $4L\sqrt n/\varepsilon\le4Lc_-^{-q/2}n^{(1+q)/2}$. Since $n^{(1+q)/2}\ge1$,
$1+4Lc_-^{-q/2}n^{(1+q)/2}\le(1+4Lc_-^{-q/2})\,n^{(1+q)/2}$, and therefore
\[
 \log_2\big(1+4L\sqrt n/\varepsilon\big)\le\tfrac{1+q}2\log_2n+\ell_0\le\tfrac32\log_2n+\ell_0\le3\log_2n
 \qquad(n\ge\max\{2,2^{2\ell_0/3}\}).
\]
For $n\ge1/(c\ln2)$ the numerator of \eqref{eq:dimension-needed} is at least $cn/2$, so
$d\ge(cn/2)/(3\log_2n)=cn/(6\log_2n)$.

label: lem:directions
title: Lemma
head: environment
name: Data processing and tracers

title: Proof
body_md:
The first three inequalities are the hierarchy of Appendix~\ref{app:hierarchy}. Conditionally on
$\widetilde Z$, the release is a function of $\widehat\theta$, and $G$ is independent of everything else, so
$U\to\widehat\theta\to X\to X+\tau G$ is a Markov chain given $\widetilde Z$. Conditional data processing gives the last
two inequalities of the first line. The same argument for the chain
$U_i\to\widehat\theta\to X_i\to X_i+\tau G_i$ given $\widetilde Z$ gives \eqref{eq:directions}; at $\tau=0$ this is the
chain recorded by \citet{wangmao2023a}.

For the tracer, note that $\sigma_i(\psi_{0,i}-\psi_{1,i})=\psi(\widehat\theta,Z^{\mathrm{tr}}_i)-\psi(\widehat\theta,Z^{\mathrm{gh}}_i)$, since
$\sigma_i=1$ exactly when $Z_{0,i}$ is the training candidate. The ghost is a fresh point, independent
of $\widehat\theta$, so $\mathbb{E}\sigma_i(\psi_{0,i}-\psi_{1,i})\ge\mathbb{P}(\psi(\widehat\theta,Z^{\mathrm{tr}}_i)=1)-\xi$, and summing over $i$,
$\sum_i\mathbb{E}\sigma_i(\psi_{0,i}-\psi_{1,i})\ge\mathrm{rec}-n\xi$; moreover $\sum_i\mathbb{E}(\psi_{0,i}-\psi_{1,i})^2\le n$.
If $\mathrm{rec}\le n\xi$ there is nothing to prove. Otherwise the fair-bit inequality \eqref{eq:fairbit}
for each pair, with the value zero for a pair whose difference vanishes almost surely, and
Cauchy--Schwarz over $i$ give
\[
 \sum_iI(\psi_{0,i}-\psi_{1,i};U_i)
 \ge\frac1{2\ln2}\sum_i\frac{(\mathbb{E}\sigma_i(\psi_{0,i}-\psi_{1,i}))^2}{\mathbb{E}(\psi_{0,i}-\psi_{1,i})^2}
 \ge\frac{(\mathrm{rec}-n\xi)^2}{2\ln2\,n}.
\]
As $\psi_{0,i}-\psi_{1,i}$ is a function of $(\psi_{0,i},\psi_{1,i})$, data processing gives the
claim.

label: lem:sign
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:sign}
Let $D$ be a law on the unit ball and let $\phi$ be strictly decreasing on $[-1,1]$. Consider a
tracer that flags $z$ when $\chi(\langle\widehat\theta,z\rangle;\widehat\theta)\ge0$, for a function $\chi(t;\theta)$ that is
strictly increasing in $t$ for every $\theta$. Centred linear scores with a threshold $c$,
$\chi(t;\theta)=t-\langle\theta,\mu_D\rangle-c$, and negative losses with a threshold $c$,
$\chi(t;\theta)=-g(\theta)-\phi(t)-c$, are of this form. If the tracer has false-positive rate at most
$\xi$ and expected training recall at least $\mathrm{rec}$ at $D$, then the decoder
$\widehat U_i=\mathbf{1}\{X_i<0\}$ satisfies $n^{-1}\sum_i\mathbb{P}(\widehat U_i=U_i)\ge\mathrm{rec}/n-\xi$, and whenever
$\mathrm{rec}/n-\xi>1/2$, with the function $\mathsf{J}$ of Appendix~\ref{app:fairbit},
\begin{equation}\label{eq:sign-transfer}
 \mathcal{I}^{\mathrm{ind}}_D(X)\ \ge\ n\,\mathsf{J}\big(2(\mathrm{rec}/n-\xi)-1\big).
\end{equation}
head: environment
name: What transfers at zero noise

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $E_i$ be the event that the tracer flags the training candidate $Z^{\mathrm{tr}}_i$ and does not flag the
ghost $Z^{\mathrm{gh}}_i$. On $E_i$, $\chi(\langle\widehat\theta,Z^{\mathrm{tr}}_i\rangle;\widehat\theta)\ge0>\chi(\langle\widehat\theta,Z^{\mathrm{gh}}_i\rangle;\widehat\theta)$, hence
$\langle\widehat\theta,Z^{\mathrm{tr}}_i\rangle>\langle\widehat\theta,Z^{\mathrm{gh}}_i\rangle$. Both margins lie in $[-1,1]$, the regularizer cancels and $\phi$
is strictly decreasing there, so $f(\widehat\theta,Z^{\mathrm{tr}}_i)<f(\widehat\theta,Z^{\mathrm{gh}}_i)$, that is, $\sigma_iX_i>0$. Thus on
$E_i$ we have $X_i>0$ if $U_i=0$ and $X_i<0$ if $U_i=1$, so $\widehat U_i=U_i$. The ghost is a fresh
point independent of $\widehat\theta$, so $\mathbb{P}(E_i)\ge\mathbb{P}(\psi(\widehat\theta,Z^{\mathrm{tr}}_i)=1)-\xi$, and summing over $i$ gives
the bound on the average success. The estimate $\widehat U_i$ is a function of $X_i$, and Fano's
inequality for the fair bit $U_i$ gives
$I(X_i;U_i)\ge I(\widehat U_i;U_i)\ge1-\mathrm{h}_2(\mathbb{P}(\widehat U_i=U_i))=\mathsf{J}(2\mathbb{P}(\widehat U_i=U_i)-1)$.
The function $\mathsf{J}$ is even and convex, and increasing on $[0,1]$, so Jensen's inequality and the bound
on the average success prove \eqref{eq:sign-transfer}.

label: lem:power-accuracy
title: Lemma
head: environment
name: Accuracy of $T_r(\Zbar)$

title: Proof
body_md:
(a) Let $\theta_x=T_r(x)$ and $\theta_{x'}=T_r(x')$, and write $\nabla g(\theta)=\lVert\theta\rVert^{r-2}\theta$.
The first-order conditions for the two minimizations on $W$ are
$\langle\nabla g(\theta_x)-x,\theta-\theta_x\rangle\ge0$ and $\langle\nabla g(\theta_{x'})-x',\theta-\theta_{x'}\rangle\ge0$
for all $\theta\in W$. Taking $\theta=\theta_{x'}$ in the first and $\theta=\theta_x$ in the second and
adding,
\[
 \langlex-x',\theta_x-\theta_{x'}\rangle\ \ge\ \langle\nabla g(\theta_x)-\nabla g(\theta_{x'}),\theta_x-\theta_{x'}\rangle
 \ \ge\ 2^{2-r}\lVert\theta_x-\theta_{x'}\rVert^r,
\]
where the last step is the monotonicity inequality of the power map (Appendix~\ref{app:power};
\citealp[Chapter~12]{lindqvist2019}). The left side is at most $\lVertx-x'\rVert\lVert\theta_x-\theta_{x'}\rVert$,
so $\lVert\theta_x-\theta_{x'}\rVert^{r-1}\le2^{r-2}\lVertx-x'\rVert$; as $1/(r-1)=q-1$ and $(r-2)/(r-1)=2-q$, this is
the second inequality. On $W$, $T_r(t)=\lVertt\rVert^{q-2}t$ for $t\ne0$, so $\lVertT_r(t)\rVert=\lVertt\rVert^{q-1}$
and $T_r(t)$ has the direction of $t$; hence $T_r(t)$ determines $t\in W$.

(b) For $\theta\in W$, $F_D(\theta)=\lVert\theta\rVert^r/r-\langle\theta,\mu_D\rangle$, so
$\min_WF_D=-g_W^{*}(\mu_D)$. Since $T_r(t)$ attains the supremum that defines $g_W^{*}(t)$, Fenchel's
equality $\lVertT_r(t)\rVert^r/r+g_W^{*}(t)=\langleT_r(t),t\rangle$ holds, and therefore
\[
 F_D(T_r(t))-\min_WF_D=\langleT_r(t),t\rangle-g_W^{*}(t)-\langleT_r(t),\mu_D\rangle+g_W^{*}(\mu_D)=D_{g_W^{*}}(\mu_D,t),
\]
because $\nablag_W^{*}(t)=T_r(t)$. Along the segment from $t$ to $\mu_D$, part~(a) gives
\[
 D_{g_W^{*}}(\mu_D,t)=\int_0^1\langleT_r(t+y(\mu_D-t))-T_r(t),\mu_D-t\rangle\,dy
 \le\int_0^12^{2-q}y^{q-1}\lVert\mu_D-t\rVert^q\,dy=c_q\lVert\mu_D-t\rVert^q .
\]

(c) As $\lVertT_r(t)\rVert\le1$ for every $t$, the learner is proper. Part~(b) with $t=\bar Z$, Jensen's
inequality ($q\le2$) and $\mathbb{E}\lVert\bar Z-\mu_D\rVert^2=(\mathbb{E}\lVertZ\rVert^2-\lVert\mu_D\rVert^2)/n\le1/n$ give
\[
 \mathbb{E} F_D(T_r(\bar Z))-\min_WF_D\le c_q\mathbb{E}\lVert\bar Z-\mu_D\rVert^q\le c_q\big(\mathbb{E}\lVert\bar Z-\mu_D\rVert^2\big)^{q/2}
 \le c_qn^{-q/2}.
\]
For $r=2$, $g_W^{*}(t)=\lVertt\rVert^2/2$ on $W$, and both $\mu_D$ and $\bar Z$ lie in $W$, so
$D_{g_W^{*}}(\mu_D,\bar Z)=\lVert\mu_D-\bar Z\rVert^2/2$ exactly.

label: lem:full-rank
title: Lemma
head: environment
name: The pair matrix has full rank

title: Proof
body_md:
(a) Let $\sigma,\sigma'$ be sign vectors, and put $t=\bar Z(\sigma)$ and $t'=\bar Z(\sigma')$; both lie
in $W$. If the two releases are equal, then $\Delta(T_r(t)-T_r(t'))=0$, so $T_r(t)-T_r(t')$ lies in
the kernel of $\Delta$, which is orthogonal to the range of $\Delta^\top$, while
$t-t'=-\Delta^\top(\sigma-\sigma')/(2n)$ lies in that range. Hence $\langlet-t',T_r(t)-T_r(t')\rangle=0$, and
Lemma~\ref{lem:power-accuracy}(a) gives $T_r(t)=T_r(t')$, so $t=t'$ by injectivity on $W$.
Conversely, equal training means give equal releases.

(b) At $D_0$ the entries of $\Delta$ are independent, and each equals $0$, $2/\sqrt d$ or $-2/\sqrt d$
with probabilities $1/2$, $1/4$ and $1/4$. A column of $\Delta$ lies in a given proper linear subspace
of $\mathbb{R}^n$ with probability at most $1/2$: choose a nonzero vector $y$ orthogonal to the subspace and an
index $i$ with $y_i\ne0$; membership forces the column to be orthogonal to $y$, which, given the
other entries of the column, fixes its $i$-th entry, and that entry takes each value with probability
at most $1/2$. The $d$ columns are independent,
so as long as the first $k$ columns span less than $\mathbb{R}^n$, column $k+1$ raises the rank with
conditional probability at least $1/2$. Call step $k+1$ a success if it raises the rank or the rank is
already $n$. Every step succeeds with conditional probability at least $1/2$, so the number of
successes stochastically dominates a $\operatorname{Bin}(d,1/2)$ variable; and if $\operatorname{rank}\Delta<n$, the successes
are exactly the rank increases, which number fewer than $n$. Hence
\[
 \mathbb{P}_0(\operatorname{rank}\Delta<n)\le\mathbb{P}\big(\operatorname{Bin}(d,1/2)<n\big)\le\mathbb{P}\big(\operatorname{Bin}(32n,1/2)<n\big)\le e^{-225n/32},
\]
where the middle step holds because $\operatorname{Bin}(d,1/2)$ is stochastically increasing in $d$, and the last is
the multiplicative Chernoff bound for the lower tail: $\operatorname{Bin}(32n,1/2)$ has mean $16n$, and
$n=(1-\tfrac{15}{16})\,16n$, so the probability is at most
$\exp\{-(\tfrac{15}{16})^2\cdot16n/2\}=e^{-225n/32}$. When $\operatorname{rank}\Delta=n$, $\Delta^\top$ is injective, so distinct sign vectors give
distinct training means and, by~(a), distinct releases; given $\widetilde Z$, the release then determines
$\sigma$ and hence $U$. Conditionally on such a supersample the information is $\mathrm{H}(U)=n$ bits, and
averaging over the supersample gives the bound.
head: environment

label: prop:separation
title: Proposition
head: environment
name: Model information does not determine the tradeoff

title: Proof
body_md:
(i) The learners are proper because $\lVert\bar Z\rVert\le1$ and $\lVertT_4(\bar Z)\rVert=\lVert\bar Z\rVert^{1/3}\le1$.
Lemma~\ref{lem:power-accuracy}(c) gives the excess risk $1/(2n)$ for $r=2$ and $c_{4/3}n^{-2/3}$ for
$r=4$, where $q=4/3$ and $c_{4/3}=2^{2/3}\cdot3/4<1.2$. So these learners reach accuracy $\varepsilon$
with $O(n_{\varepsilon})$ samples, $n_{\varepsilon}=\varepsilon^{-2/q}$, and by Proposition~\ref{prop:samples} every proper
learner that is $\varepsilon$-accurate on the family needs $\Omega(n_{\varepsilon})$ samples when $d\geC_{\mathrm{dim}}n_{\varepsilon}$ and
$\varepsilon$ is small.

(ii) The map $T_4$ is a bijection of $W$ onto itself, with inverse $\theta\mapsto\lVert\theta\rVert^2\theta$, and
both maps are continuous. Since $\widehat\theta^{(4)}=T_4(\widehat\theta^{(2)})$ pointwise, each output is a measurable
bijective image of the other, so every mutual information between the model and the selection bits,
conditional on $\widetilde Z$ or not, is the same for both learners. (The unconditional one is zero for every
learner, since the law of the training set does not depend on $U$.) If $\psi$ is a tracer for
$\widehat\theta^{(2)}$, then $\psi'(\theta,z)=\psi(T_4^{-1}(\theta),z)$ makes the same decisions for $\widehat\theta^{(4)}$,
and conversely with $T_4$ in place of $T_4^{-1}$.

For the noiseless releases, Lemma~\ref{lem:full-rank}(a), with $r=2$ (where $T_2(\bar Z)=\bar Z$) and
with $r=4$, shows that on every supersample $X^{(2)}$ and $X^{(4)}$ induce the same partition of the
sign vectors as the training mean does, including on supersamples where $\Delta$ has rank below $n$.
Given $\widetilde Z$, both releases are functions of $U$, and the information between $U$ and a function of
$U$ depends only on the partition that the function induces; hence
$I(X^{(2)};U\mid\widetilde Z)=I(X^{(4)};U\mid\widetilde Z)=I(\bar Z;U\mid\widetilde Z)$ exactly. At $D_0$,
Lemma~\ref{lem:full-rank}(b) bounds this common value from below by $n(1-e^{-225n/32})$, and by
Lemma~\ref{lem:directions} the common model information is at least as large.

(iii) This is the bound for the mean learner proved in Appendix~\ref{app:growth}.

(iv) At $D_0$, $\sigma_iX^{(4)}_i=\langle\widehat\theta^{(4)},Z^{\mathrm{tr}}_i-Z^{\mathrm{gh}}_i\rangle$, and the ghost is independent of
$(\widehat\theta^{(4)},Z^{\mathrm{tr}}_i)$ with mean zero. So the signed mean is
\[
 M^{(4)}:=\sum_i\mathbb{E}_0\sigma_iX^{(4)}_i=\mathbb{E}_0\langleT_4(\bar Z),n\bar Z\rangle=n\,\mathbb{E}_0\lVert\bar Z\rVert^{4/3}.
\]
Expand $\lVertn\bar Z\rVert^2=n+2\sum_{i<j}\langleZ^{\mathrm{tr}}_i,Z^{\mathrm{tr}}_j\rangle$. The cross terms are uncorrelated, with
mean zero and $\mathbb{E}_0\langleZ^{\mathrm{tr}}_i,Z^{\mathrm{tr}}_j\rangle^2=1/d$, so $\mathbb{E}_0\lVert\bar Z\rVert^2=1/n$ and
$\mathbb{E}_0\lVert\bar Z\rVert^4=n^{-4}\big(n^2+2n(n-1)/d\big)\le n^{-2}(1+2/d)$. Cauchy--Schwarz,
$\mathbb{E}_0\lVert\bar Z\rVert^2=\mathbb{E}_0[\lVert\bar Z\rVert^{2/3}\lVert\bar Z\rVert^{4/3}]\le(\mathbb{E}_0\lVert\bar Z\rVert^{4/3}\,\mathbb{E}_0\lVert\bar Z\rVert^{8/3})^{1/2}$,
and Jensen's inequality, $\mathbb{E}_0\lVert\bar Z\rVert^{8/3}\le(\mathbb{E}_0\lVert\bar Z\rVert^4)^{2/3}$, give
$\mathbb{E}_0\lVert\bar Z\rVert^{4/3}\ge n^{-2/3}(1+2/d)^{-2/3}$, hence $M^{(4)}\ge n^{1/3}(1+2/d)^{-2/3}$.

For the energy, $V^{(4)}:=\sum_i\mathbb{E}_0(X^{(4)}_i)^2=\mathbb{E}_0\lVert\Delta T_4(\bar Z)\rVert^2
\le\mathbb{E}_0\big[\lVert\Delta\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}^2\lVert\bar Z\rVert^{2/3}\big]$. The weight $\lVert\bar Z\rVert^{2/3}$ is at most one, and
$\mathbb{E}_0\lVert\bar Z\rVert^{2/3}\le(\mathbb{E}_0\lVert\bar Z\rVert^2)^{1/3}=n^{-1/3}$ by Jensen's inequality.
Lemma~\ref{lem:weighted} with the pair-matrix tail of Lemma~\ref{lem:matrix} gives
\[
 V^{(4)}\le\mathfrak{T}_1(n^{-1/3};2K_0,2K_1)=n^{-1/3}\big\{2K_0+2K_1\big[1+\tfrac13\ln n\big]\big\}<4.2\,n^{-1/3},
\]
because for $n\ge16$ and $d\ge32n$, $2K_0<4.062$ and $2K_1\le0.282/n$, and
$4.062+0.282\,(1+\tfrac13\ln16)/16<4.1$.

The fair-bit inequality \eqref{eq:fairbit} for each coordinate $X^{(4)}_i+\tau G_i$, whose signed mean
is $\mathbb{E}_0\sigma_iX^{(4)}_i$ and whose second moment is $\mathbb{E}_0(X^{(4)}_i)^2+\tau^2$, followed by
Cauchy--Schwarz over $i$ as in Appendix~\ref{app:fairbit}, gives
$\mathcal{I}^{\mathrm{ind}}_{D_0}(X^{(4)}+\tau G)\ge(M^{(4)})^2/(2\ln2\,(V^{(4)}+n\tau^2))$. This is the lower bound of
Theorem~\ref{thm:transfer} at the single law $D_0$, and with the two estimates above it is
\eqref{eq:separation-lower}.

(v) At $\tau=n^{-2/3}$, $n\tau^2=n^{-1/3}$. By~(iii) the first release has $\mathcal{I}^{\mathrm{cand}}_{D_p}\le3n^{1/3}$ at
every $p$. By~(iv) the second has $\mathcal{I}^{\mathrm{ind}}_{D_0}\ge n(1+2/d)^{-4/3}/(2\ln2\cdot5.2)\ge n/8$, since
$d\ge32n\ge512$. The chain \eqref{eq:hierarchy} transfers the upper bound to $\mathcal{I}^{\mathrm{ind}}$ and $\mathcal{I}^{\mathrm{joint}}$, and the
lower bound to $\mathcal{I}^{\mathrm{joint}}$ and $\mathcal{I}^{\mathrm{cand}}$.

label: lem:ridge-moments
title: Lemma
head: environment
name: Exact moments of ridge ERM

title: Proof
body_md:
Under $D_p$ the $2nd$ coordinates $Z_{j,i,k}$ are independent, with $Z_{j,i,k}^2=1/d$ and mean
$p_k/\sqrt d$. So $\Delta_1,\dots,\Delta_n$ are independent, with independent centred coordinates,
$\mathbb{E}_p\Delta_{i,k}^2=2(1-p_k^2)/d$ and $\mathbb{E}_p\lVert\Delta_i\rVert^2=2(1-\lVert\mu_p\rVert^2)$; the signs $\sigma_j$
are fair, independent of each other and of $\widetilde Z$.
(a)~$X_i=-\langle\bar Z,\Delta_i\rangle$, and $\bar Z=z_c-(2n)^{-1}\sum_j\sigma_j\Delta_j$ since
$Z_{U_j,j}=(Z_{0,j}+Z_{1,j}-\sigma_j\Delta_j)/2$.
(b)~By (a), $\mathbb{E}_p\sigma_iX_i=(2n)^{-1}\mathbb{E}_p\lVert\Delta_i\rVert^2$; sum over $i$ and use \eqref{eq:gap}.
(c)~By (a), $\mathbb{E}_p(X_i-x_i(\widetilde Z))^2=(4n^2)^{-1}\sum_j\mathbb{E}_p\langle\Delta_j,\Delta_i\rangle^2$. For $j\ne i$ the term
is $\sum_k(\mathbb{E}_p\Delta_{i,k}^2)^2=4d^{-2}\sum_k(1-p_k^2)^2=4(1-\lVert\mu_p\rVert^2-\Gamma_p)/d$. For $j=i$,
$\Delta_{i,k}^2=4B_k/d$, where the indicators $B_k$ that the two candidates differ in coordinate $k$
are independent with mean $(1-p_k^2)/2$ and variance $(1-p_k^4)/4$, so
$\mathbb{E}_p\lVert\Delta_i\rVert^4=16d^{-2}[(\sum_k(1-p_k^2)/2)^2+\sum_k(1-p_k^4)/4]
=4(1-\lVert\mu_p\rVert^2)^2+4(1-\lVert\mu_p\rVert^2+\Gamma_p)/d$. Sum over $j$ and $i$.
(d)~By (a), $\mathbb{E}_pX_i^2=\mathbb{E}_p(X_i-x_i(\widetilde Z))^2+\mathbb{E}_px_i(\widetilde Z)^2$. As $\lVertZ_{0,i}\rVert=\lVertZ_{1,i}\rVert$,
$\langleZ_{0,i}+Z_{1,i},\Delta_i\rangle=0$, so $x_i(\widetilde Z)=-(2n)^{-1}\langleR_i,\Delta_i\rangle$, where $R_i$, the sum of
the $N=2(n-1)$ candidates outside pair $i$, is independent of $\Delta_i$. With
$\mathbb{E}_pR_{i,k}^2=N/d+N(N-1)p_k^2/d$ this gives
$\mathbb{E}_px_i(\widetilde Z)^2=(n-1)[1-\lVert\mu_p\rVert^2+(2n-3)\Gamma_p]/(n^2d)$. Neither term depends on $i$; summing
over $i$ gives (d).

label: rem:affine
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:affine}
For the affine link $\phi(t)=-t$, the link remainder $u$ of Step~3 in Section~\ref{sec:moments}
vanishes and $\sigma_iX_i=\langle\widehat\theta,Z^{\mathrm{tr}}_i-Z^{\mathrm{gh}}_i\rangle$. The ghost is independent of $\widehat\theta$ and has mean
$\mu_p$, so the signed mean is $\mathbb{E}_p\langle\widehat\theta,\sum_i(Z^{\mathrm{tr}}_i-\mu_p)\rangle$, and Lemma~\ref{lem:fp} turns
its prior average into $\kappa\,\mathbb{E}_\Pi\langle\widehat\theta,\mu_p\rangle$. Earlier lower bounds for the model rest on
the same argument. The identity of Lemma~\ref{lem:fp} is the beta-prior fingerprinting lemma of
\citet{steinke2017}; it is Lemma~3.8 of \citet{voitovych2025} when the sparsity of their data equals
the dimension, and Lemma~6.3 of \citet{attias2024} rests on an identity of the same kind with a
uniform prior. Accuracy enters through the
alignment $\mathbb{E}\langle\widehat\theta,\mu_p\rangle$. On the affine instance of \citet[Section~6.1.1]{attias2024}, which
has no regularizer, their Lemma~6.2 gives $\mathbb{E}\langle\widehat\theta,\mu_D\rangle\ge\lVert\mu_D\rVert-\varepsilon-2\delta'$, where
$\mu_D$ is the mean of the data law $D$, for learners whose excess risk exceeds $\varepsilon$ with
probability at most $\delta'$, and
\citet[Proposition~E.1]{voitovych2025} give the analogue for parameters in a cube. The energy bound
rests on the operator norm of the centred training matrix (Lemma~\ref{lem:matrix}), as does
Lemma~A.7 of \citet{attias2024}. With the ridge regularizer, the loss
$f_2(\theta,z)=\lVert\theta\rVert^2/2-\langle\theta,z\rangle$ is the strongly convex instance of
\citet[Section~7.1.1]{attias2024} restricted to the unit ball, and their Lemma~7.1 contains the
localization $\lVert\widehat\theta-\mu_D\rVert^2\le2\varepsilon$, which holds there with probability at least $1-\delta'$,
and their Lemma~7.3 the signed moment used here. For $f_2$, therefore, the moment bounds behind the lower
half of Theorem~\ref{thm:main} are of a known kind, and Theorem~\ref{thm:transfer} turns them into the
lower half at every noise level. The recall bounds of \citet[Theorem~3.5]{voitovych2025} rest on the
same two moments, the signed mean and the energy, which a counting inequality (their Lemma~A.11)
turns into recall. What Theorem~\ref{thm:main} adds lies elsewhere: the moment bounds for nonlinear
links and matched power curvature, where calibration through the upper growth and localization at
every law keep the train--ghost remainder \eqref{eq:taylor-main} below the signal, and
Proposition~\ref{prop:growth} shows that the upper growth cannot be dropped; the residual bound at
every law, which gives the upper half; and the two-sided dependence on $\tau$ that follows.

body_md:
Information is measured in bits: \nolinkurl{mutualInfo} is the Kullback--Leibler divergence of the
joint law from the product of the marginals, divided by $\ln2$, with the convention that an infinite
divergence gives $0$, and \nolinkurl{condMutualInfo} defines conditional information by the chain rule,
$I(A;B\mid C)=I(A;(B,C))-I(A;C)$. Every information in the formal statements is an information about
selection bits, which are uniform on a finite set; for these the divergence is finite
(\nolinkurl{mutualInfoNats_ne_top_of_uniform}), so the convention never applies. The three
information measures of the release lie in $[0,n]$ at every law of the family, and the worst case
$\sup_p\mathcal{Q}_{D_p}(X+\tau G)$ is their supremum over $p\in[-1,1]^d$ as a real number
(\nolinkurl{nativeWorstInformation}). The class \nolinkurl{nativeAccurateLearners} consists of the
jointly measurable proper learners that are $\varepsilon$-accurate on the family, as in
Section~\ref{sec:setting}. The formal statements also carry the measurability and integrability
conditions that the text leaves implicit.
